suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Destructured first destination is dereferenced without optional chaining, crashing EventManager.create when destinationCalendar is null/[] and location is Google Meet.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without a null guard after `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty. WHY: handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (and handleCancelBooking/confirm/editLocation/webhooks all set `[]`), so any booking with location Google Meet (MeetLocationType) and no configured destination calendar — a very common setup — crashes event creation with an unhandled TypeError (old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was null-safe). HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Optional-chained push silently drops all team hosts' destination calendars when the organizer has none, defeating the PR's collective multi-host feature.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null, which happens at lines 1063-1067 when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar is set. WHY: for COLLECTIVE team bookings — the exact scenario this PR implements (Fixes #7754) — the destination calendars collected from users.slice(1) at lines 987-994 are silently dropped, so EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents falls back to the organizer's first connected calendar and the other hosts never get the event on their calendars. HOW: assign instead of optionally pushing: `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];` (or default `destinationCalendar` to `[]` at 1063-1067).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateLocation's references always store undefined externalCalendarId/credentialId because CalendarManager.updateEvent never returns those fields.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` read fields that CalendarManager.updateEvent never returns (its return object at CalendarManager.ts:313-322 contains only appName/type/success/uid/updatedEvent/originalEvent/calError/calWarnings), so both are always undefined for calendar results. WHY: editLocation.handler.ts:119-121 creates booking references from `updatedResult.referencesToCreate`, so every reference created after a location edit loses the external calendar id and credential id that the old code took from `evt.destinationCalendar`; subsequent reschedules (updateAllCalendarEvents) and cancellations (handleCancelBooking) then take the legacy all-credentials branch and send an undefined calendarId to GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, failing to target the right calendar. HOW: add `externalId: externalCalendarId, credentialId: credential.id` to CalendarManager.updateEvent's return (mirroring the new createEvent return), or restore the `evt.destinationCalendar` fallback in the mapping.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback find() compares externalId against a falsy externalCalendarId so it never matches, sending undefined/primary as calendarId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares each externalId against undefined/null and can never match, always yielding undefined — the old code returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. WHY: in updateEvent the result is passed as `calendarId: selectedCalendar` (line 261) with no "primary" fallback, so a reschedule/update on any booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (references created by this PR's no-credentialId branch or by editLocation) sends calendarId undefined and the Google call fails; in deleteEvent (315-317) it falls back to "primary" (line 322), so deleting an event that lives on a non-primary destination calendar 404s and is silently resolved (lines 333-335), leaving an orphaned event on the real calendar. HOW: fall back to the first destination instead, e.g. `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId || event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId;` in updateEvent (adding `|| "primary"` at the call) and `const calendarId = externalCalendarId || event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId || defaultCalendarId;` in deleteEvent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: createEvent now requires destinationCalendar.credentialId to match, so destinations with null credentialId are created on "primary" and their reference loses externalCalendarId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` requires a destinationCalendar row whose credentialId equals the creating credential's id; destinations with a null credentialId — a state the old EventManager explicitly supported via its `if (event.destinationCalendar.credentialId)` else-branch, which this PR keeps at EventManager.ts:375-382 — never match, so the event is inserted into "primary" instead of the user's selected destination calendar. WHY: additionally that else-branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the externalId argument, so CalendarManager.createEvent returns externalId undefined and EventManager.create (line 169) stores a booking reference with externalCalendarId undefined — old code stored `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` — so subsequent updates/deletes can no longer locate the event on the destination calendar. HOW: fall back to the credentialId-less destination (e.g. `?.externalId ?? calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => !cal.credentialId)?.externalId`) and pass `destination.externalId` at EventManager.ts:379-381 so the reference keeps the correct calendar id.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Office365 (and Lark/BaseCalendarService) always use destinationCalendar[0].externalId, so a non-first collective host's event is created against the wrong host's calendar id.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` plus `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` always selects the FIRST host's destination calendar, even when EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (EventManager.ts:339-374) is creating the event with a second host's credential — unlike GoogleCalendarService, whose createEvent was updated to select the destination matching the passed credentialId. WHY: for COLLECTIVE team events with mixed providers (host 1 on Google, host 2 on Office365/Lark/caldav), the Office365 create uses host 1's Google externalId in `/me/calendars/{id}/events` → Graph 404 and the host-2 calendar event fails; LarkCalendarService.createEvent/createAttendees (lines 128-129, 164-165) has the same hard-coded first-destination selection, and BaseCalendarService (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-164) filters its calendars by the first destination's externalId, matching none and creating the event on no calendar. HOW: accept the credentialId parameter already added to the Calendar interface (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221) and resolve the destination like Google does: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId ?? event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` — apply the same fix in larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The recurring-cancellation deletion fan-out now runs once per calendar reference, deleting each remaining booking's events N times.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `bookingCalendarReference` changed from a single reference (find) to an array (filter) and the whole delete loop at 423-483 runs per reference, but the recurring-cancellation branch (444-468) iterates ALL of the user's calendar credentials × all updatedBookings regardless of which reference is being processed. WHY: for multi-host bookings created by this PR (one calendar reference per host destination), the recurring branch executes N times and pushes duplicate delete calls into apiDeletes — each remaining booking's calendar events are deleted N times, producing duplicate rejected promises (404/410) and noisy error logs during cancellation of a recurring series. HOW: hoist the recurring branch out of the per-reference loop (it only needs to run once), e.g. guard it with a boolean or check `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && ...` before the loop and keep only the single-delete path (469-471) inside it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Missing optional chaining on the newly destructured first destination calendar crashes EventManager.create when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The array migration dropped the optional chaining that made the Google-Meet fallback null-safe. Line 118 `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` produces `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or an empty array, and line 119 then dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no `?.`, throwing a TypeError. This PR itself makes that state reachable: handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 now explicitly assigns `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (e.g. users with only Cal Video and no calendar integration), and bookingReminder.ts:130, packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:119/229, confirm.handler.ts:175-179, editLocation.handler.ts:85-89 all pass `[]`. Any such booking with a Google Meet location now throws in EventManager.create instead of falling back to Cal Video, failing the entire booking creation request. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google updateEvent's rewritten fallback (`find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy) can never match, so rescheduling bookings without an externalCalendarId reference fails.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The updateEvent fallback lost its coverage of the missing-externalCalendarId case during the array migration. The expression `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` sits in the branch taken when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), so the predicate compares each calendar's externalId against undefined/null and can never match — the result is always undefined. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which resolved the destination calendar for exactly these bookings. Callers hit this via EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents (calenderExternalId is null whenever the booking's `_calendar` reference lacks externalCalendarId — including all references this PR now creates through the no-credentialId branch, where CalendarManager.createEvent is called without externalId and returns `externalId: undefined`), and `calendar.events.update` then runs with an undefined calendarId and throws (missing required parameter / wrong calendar). Fix: fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or match by credentialId) instead of find-by-externalCalendarId in the falsy branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google deleteEvent's rewritten fallback can never match when externalCalendarId is absent, so cancelling those bookings fails instead of deleting the event from the configured calendar.
suggestions.suggestionContent: deleteEvent has the same broken fallback as updateEvent: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `find` compares each externalId against undefined/null and never matches; calendarId is always undefined there. Depending on the final call, this either throws for the missing required `calendarId` or falls back to "primary" and 404s because the event lives on the configured destination calendar. Old code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which resolved the correct calendar. Callers reach this from handleCancelBooking.ts:424-480 (and EventManager delete paths) for any booking whose `_calendar` reference has no externalCalendarId — including references created by this PR itself via the no-credentialId branch. Fix: fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or match by credentialId) when externalCalendarId is absent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google createEvent now only matches destinations by credentialId, so destinations with null credentialId silently create the event on "primary" instead of their configured externalId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: createEvent now resolves the target calendar solely via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. DestinationCalendar rows with a null credentialId are still a supported case in this PR (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents keeps the else branch that filters credentials by `destination.integration` and calls createEvent without a credentialId on the destination, EventManager.ts:376-381), so for those destinations the find never matches and the event is silently created on "primary" instead of the destination's configured externalId — the old code used `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId` with "primary" only as a last resort. Because that branch also never passes `destination.externalId` into CalendarManager.createEvent, the stored booking reference gets no externalCalendarId, compounding the update/delete fallback failures. Consider falling back to the destination externalId whose integration matches this credential (or the caller-supplied externalId) before defaulting to "primary".

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: createEvent's rewritten catch block logs the full CalendarEvent (attendee PII, booking notes) and this PR makes it run once per destination calendar, multiplying PII in logs.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The catch block rewritten by this PR logs the entire calEvent object: `log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent)` serializes attendee names/emails, additionalNotes (answers to booking questions), responses, and the destinationCalendar list into the production error log. This change also multiplies how often it fires — EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates every destinationCalendar (including each collective team host's calendar) and calls createEvent per destination, so every failed calendar write emits a full PII dump per destination (before, it ran once per booking with the single cached credential). Log only stable identifiers (uid, title, eventTypeId, integration types) instead of the full event payload.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new loadUsers catch block forwards raw Prisma error messages (internal DB/query details) to the API client in a 400 response.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new try/catch wrapping loadUsers rethrows Prisma errors as `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. PrismaClientKnownRequestError messages are of the form "Invalid `prisma.user.findMany()` invocation: ..." and can embed constraint names, raw database error text, and internal query details; those now go directly into the JSON response body exposed to the booking client. Before this change, a Prisma failure escaped loadUsers to the outer handler without this passthrough. Treat Prisma errors like the generic branch: log server-side and return a generic message (and a 5xx status — a server-side DB failure is not a client 400).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Meet-location bookings crash with TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty because the destructured value is used without optional chaining.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 119 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no null guard. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]` — which handleNewBooking produces (`... : null` at its lines 1063-1067) and every other new call site produces (`x ? [x] : []`) — destructuring `[]` yields `undefined`, and the property access throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` for any booking whose location is MeetLocationType. The old code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) safely fell back to Cal Video for exactly this scenario; now the booking request 500s instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateEvent's fallback searches destinationCalendar for an externalId equal to the already-known-falsy externalCalendarId, so it always yields undefined and calendar.events.update is called with calendarId: undefined.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `else` branch of `selectedCalendar` is dead, self-negating computation: it is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it then searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. equal to that falsy value), so the find can never yield a usable calendar id. `selectedCalendar` ends up `undefined` and `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined })` fails, so Google events for bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings, or new bookings created through EventManager's no-credentialId branch which calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the externalId argument) can no longer be rescheduled. The pre-refactor code correctly fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: deleteEvent's fallback is the same dead find (compares against the falsy externalCalendarId), silently degrading to deleting from 'primary' so events in the real destination calendar are never removed.
suggestions.suggestionContent: deleteEvent (lines 315-317) repeats the same self-negating find (`cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy), so `calendarId` is always falsy in the fallback. Because of the `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` guard on line 322, the deletion silently degrades to `"primary"` instead of the destination calendar — cancelling such a booking attempts to delete from the user's primary calendar, gets a 404 (silently resolved on line 335), and leaves the real event on the destination calendar. Old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and deleted the correct event.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: office365/lark/BaseCalendarService always use destinationCalendar[0] while EventManager now creates one event per destination with that destination's credential, so mixed-integration collective events target the wrong calendar and the stored reference externalId disagrees with where the event was actually created.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This PR makes EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents iterate every entry of the (now array) destinationCalendar, invoking the matching credential per destination, and handleNewBooking now pushes each COLLECTIVE team member's destination calendar. But office365 (line 73-77), lark (lines 128-129) and BaseCalendarService (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts 156-164) all unconditionally pick `destinationCalendar[0]` (the organizer's destination) instead of the entry matching the credential that is actually creating the event — only Google's createEvent matches by credentialId. For a collective event whose organizer uses Google and a member uses Office365/Lark, the member's service is handed the organizer's Google externalId (e.g. `/me/calendars/{google-id}/events`), the request fails and the member's calendar event is never created; meanwhile CalendarManager records `externalId: destination.externalId` (the member's destination) in the booking reference even though [0] was used — the stored reference points at a different calendar than the one the event went to, breaking later updates/deletes.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: New DB-wide credential lookup by raw stored credentialId turns a previously fail-closed credential derivation into a fail-open one with no ownership or validity check.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new credential-from-DB fallback (packages/core/EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents ~343-368 and the identical block in updateAllCalendarEvents ~515-541) loads a credential row by raw stored ID (`destination.credentialId` / `reference.credentialId`) and uses it — including its OAuth tokens — to create/update calendar events, with no validation that the credential belongs to a user involved in the event (organizer/hosts) and without rejecting credentials whose `invalid` flag is set. Before this PR the lookup was confined to the booking-scoped `calendarCredentials` lists and unmatched IDs were skipped (fail-closed). Add an ownership check: only accept the fetched credential if its `userId`/`teamId` matches a host of the event (or the booking's user), and skip `invalid` credentials.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Cancellation path now fetches any credential row from the database by the reference's stored credentialId and uses it to delete calendar events, with no ownership or validity check.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same unscoped credential derivation as EventManager: handleCancelBooking (~431-441) now falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` when the reference's credentialId is not among bookingToDelete.user.credentials, then uses that credential (its OAuth tokens) via getCalendar() to delete calendar events. Previously a missing credential simply skipped deletion (fail-closed). Guard the fallback: only use the fetched credential if it belongs to the booking's user/hosts (userId/teamId check) and skip it when `invalid` is true.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Meet-location fallback crashes with TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty because mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration is dereferenced without optional chaining.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Null/empty destinationCalendar crashes the Google Meet fallback. `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` produces `undefined` when destinationCalendar is null (handleNewBooking's `: null` fallback) or `[]` (cancel/confirm/webhook handlers pass `[]`), and line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This throws exactly in the scenario the fallback was written for — Google Meet location selected with no Google calendar destination — aborting booking creation with a TypeError. Old code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) was null-safe. Fix: add optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateEvent/deleteEvent's fallback find can never match because it compares externalId against a falsy externalCalendarId, leaving calendarId undefined and breaking reschedule/cancel for bookings without a stored externalCalendarId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: updateEvent's (and deleteEvent's, lines ~314-317) new fallback is dead code: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares real calendar IDs to null/undefined and never matches — selectedCalendar/calendarId is always undefined, unlike the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. This PR itself produces such references: EventManager's else-branch calls createEvent without an externalId, so references are saved with null externalCalendarId; rescheduling/cancelling those bookings calls google events.update/delete with `calendarId: undefined`, which googleapis rejects as a missing required parameter (inside `new Promise(async ...)` the outer promise never settles → hang / failed update). Fix the fallback to use a credential/integration match or the first destination calendar instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: createEvent falls back to "primary" instead of the configured destination calendar when the destination row has no credentialId, placing events on the wrong calendar and duplicating across same-type credentials.
suggestions.suggestionContent: createEvent silently creates events on the wrong calendar when a destination calendar has no credentialId. EventManager's fallback branch (destination.credentialId falsy) ends up calling createEvent where `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` never matches, so `calendarId` falls back to "primary" — the event lands on the credential's primary calendar instead of the user's configured destination calendar, and is duplicated on every same-type credential's primary (old code used destinationCalendar.externalId and relied on the CalendarManager 404-catch to skip non-owning credentials). It also stores externalCalendarId: undefined in the reference, which feeds the broken update/delete fallback. Fall back to the destination row for the integration instead of always defaulting to "primary".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: evt.destinationCalendar falls back to null instead of an empty array, so the COLLECTIVE team-calendar push silently no-ops and team members' destination calendars are dropped.
suggestions.suggestionContent: evt.destinationCalendar falls back to `null` (not `[]`), so when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destinationCalendar, the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op and COLLECTIVE team members' destination calendars are dropped — their events are never created on their calendars, defeating the multi-destination behavior this PR adds. Defaulting to `[]` also keeps the object in the shape downstream code (EventManager.ts:118) destructures. Fix: use `[]` as the ternary fallback (or build the array including team calendars before assigning).

suggestions.label: Add unit tests for uncovered behavioural changes
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The reviewer explicitly identifies a coverage gap: the PR adds no unit tests for the multi-destination loop in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, the credential DB fallback, or the Google selectedCalendar find-by-credentialId logic, but explicitly states this is not their assigned class and reports no findings for their class.
suggestions.suggestionContent: PR modifies packages/core/CalendarManager.ts createEvent (lines 218-270, now taking externalId and passing credential.id to calendar.createEvent, returning externalId/credentialId in the result), packages/core/EventManager.ts (lines 100-250, referencesToCreate now sourced from result.externalId/result.credentialId rather than evt.destinationCalendar), and packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (lines 72-92, destructuring the first entry of the destinationCalendar array), but adds no unit tests for the multi-destination loop in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, the credential DB fallback, or the Google selectedCalendar find-by-credentialId logic. Add unit tests to cover these behavioural changes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: EventManager.create throws TypeError on Google Meet events whose destinationCalendar is null/empty, because the array migration dropped the old null-safe optional chaining.
suggestions.suggestionContent: EventManager.create dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a guard. The `?? []` only handles `null` destinationCalendar — it cannot make an empty array produce a first element, so when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `[]` (emitted by this PR's producer hunks in webhook.ts:119, paypal-webhook.ts:152-156, bookingReminder.ts:130, confirm.handler.ts:175-179, editLocation.handler.ts:85-89, handleCancelBooking.ts:251-255) or `null` (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067), destructuring yields `undefined` and the dereference throws. This crashes the exact case the fallback exists for ("Google Meet selected w/o a Google Cal", per the comment on line 116): booking creation and Stripe/PayPal payment confirmation throw TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Restore the null-safety the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` had: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google updateEvent/deleteEvent's new destination-calendar fallback can never match, so reschedule/cancel of bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls Google with calendarId undefined.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is dead code: it only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the ternary guard), and then it compares each destination's externalId against that falsy value, so it can never match — `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined` in the fallback case and is passed to `calendar.events.update` as `calendarId` (line 261) with no `|| "primary"` (unlike createEvent line 154). The producer side of this PR still relies on that fallback: EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents (packages/core/EventManager.ts:505-510) forwards `calenderExternalId = null` whenever a booking reference lacks externalCalendarId, and this PR's referencesToCreate hunk (EventManager.ts:169) creates exactly such references in the else-branch. Reschedules and cancels of those bookings now call Google with `calendarId: undefined` and fail, where the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback worked. Same self-nullifying expression in deleteEvent (lines 314-317), reached from handleCancelBooking.ts. Fix: fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId (as the organizer-email code above does) or to "primary".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: createAllCalendarEvents' else-branch drops the destination's externalId from both the created event and the stored reference, so Google bypasses the user's chosen calendar and later updates have no calendarId to fall back on.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In createAllCalendarEvents' else-branch (destinationCalendar without credentialId), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the externalId argument while the same PR changed referencesToCreate (line 169) to store `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` instead of the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. CalendarManager.createEvent (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:267) returns `externalId` = the omitted parameter, i.e. undefined, so the booking reference is persisted with a null externalCalendarId even though the destination row carries an externalId. At the same time GoogleCalendarService.createEvent (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-154) selects the target calendar solely via `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`; a destination with no credentialId never matches, so the event is created on "primary" rather than the user's selected destination.externalId (the old code used destinationCalendar.externalId). Net effect: the chosen calendar is bypassed and later update/delete of these bookings hits the dead fallback in Google's updateEvent/deleteEvent and fails. Pass `destination.externalId` in this branch too (and have Google's createEvent fall back to the destination's externalId when no credentialId match exists).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Office365 (and Lark/CalDav) createEvent always targets destinationCalendar[0], so this PR's per-host COLLECTIVE loop creates/fails other hosts' events against the wrong calendar id.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This hunk converts Office365's createEvent to the array shape but hardcodes `destinationCalendar[0]`'s externalId, ignoring the `credentialId` the Calendar interface (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221, changed in this PR) now passes. The producer side of this PR makes that premise wrong: handleNewBooking.ts:987-1006 + 1077-1079 now pushes every COLLECTIVE host's destinationCalendar into evt.destinationCalendar, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-373) iterates them, invoking each host's own credential. For a collective event with two Office 365 hosts, host B's invocation uses B's credential but still builds `/me/calendars/{host A's externalId}/events` (CalendarService.ts:73-77) → Graph 404 with B's token → CalendarManager's catch swallows it with success=false → host B's calendar silently never receives the event while emails go out. Google's implementation in this same PR selects by credentialId (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:147-149); Office365 (and larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:127-129, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-166) should match the destination whose credentialId equals the passed one instead of always taking [0].

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Blacklisted guest emails can be bypassed by submitting the same address with different letter casing, because the blacklist is lowercased but the guest email is not.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The guest-email blacklist is bypassable via case variation: line 71 lowercases every entry of BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS, but line 77 checks !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) with the raw guest string — neither the trpc schema (addGuests.schema.ts, z.array(z.string().email())) nor the client (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) normalises the submitted email. An operator who blacklists internal@example.com can be bypassed by submitting Internal@Example.com: the guest passes the filter, is created as a booking attendee, receives the calendar/video-call invite and the notification emails. Normalise the guest email (toLowerCase) before comparing it to the lowercased blacklist.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Case-sensitive and missing-in-server duplicate handling lets the same guest email be added twice (or twice in different casing) in one request.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The uniqueness guarantee ("emails_must_be_unique_valid") is not actually enforced server-side: line 76 compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively against existing attendees, and neither the server schema nor the handler checks for duplicates among the submitted guests themselves — the duplicate-email refine exists only in the client (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29) and is itself case-sensitive, so it accepts ["a@x.com","A@x.com"]. Both variants pass the handler's filter and createMany inserts two attendee rows for the same person, producing duplicate calendar invites and duplicate emails. Compare emails case-insensitively and de-duplicate the submitted list before insert.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with &&, so it actually requires the user to be both admin AND owner, contradicting its name and over-restricting the permission check.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The boolean is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&`, so it is only true when the user is BOTH a team admin AND a team owner. The name promises that either role suffices, but an admin who is not an owner fails the check at line 54 and gets FORBIDDEN. Change the operator to `||` (or rename the variable to match the stricter semantics), so the identifier and the behaviour agree.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded English, bypassing the t() translation used by the adjacent string in the same component.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The "Remove email" tooltip content is a hard-coded English string shown to the user, while the same component imports useLocale and translates the neighbouring string with t("add_another") at line 69. This bypasses the translation mechanism: non-English users see untranslated English. Add a key (e.g. "remove_email") to the locale files this PR already touches and render it via t().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Error message key "you_do_not_have_permission" thrown by the new handler has no entry in en/common.json (verified by grep), so the error toast renders the raw untranslated key.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler throws message "you_do_not_have_permission", which the client displays via t(err.message) in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43, but grep of apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json shows no such key (unlike "booking_not_found" at line 422, which does exist). Users will see the raw key 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission' in the toast. Add the key to common.json (which this PR already extends for its other new messages) or reuse an existing permission-denied key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Server error "emails_must_be_unique_valid" fires when all guests are already attendees or blacklisted — by then the emails are already validated unique and valid, so the message shown to the user is false.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The error thrown when uniqueGuests is empty claims "Emails must be unique and valid", but at that point the emails have already passed client-side uniqueness/email validation (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29,52) and zod's z.string().email() (addGuests.schema.ts:5). The emails ARE unique and valid; the actual reason for the failure is that every submitted guest is already an attendee of the booking or is blacklisted. The user-facing message therefore disagrees with the real state — use a message that describes the actual condition (e.g. a "guests_already_added" key) so users are not told their valid, unique input is invalid.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Case-sensitive comparisons against a lowercased blacklist and case-sensitive attendee lookup let blocked or already-added emails through with different letter casing.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist is lowercased (line 71) but guest emails are compared verbatim: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and `guest === attendee.email` are case-sensitive, so "Attacker@Evil.com" bypasses a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry of "attacker@evil.com", and a case-variant of an already-added attendee slips past the duplicate filter and gets inserted. Normalize both sides (and the guest list itself) to lowercase before comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The handler never dedupes the guests array and re-checks attendees in a read-then-write window, so duplicate or concurrent submissions either crash with an unhandled Prisma unique-constraint error or create duplicate attendee rows.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The server never enforces the uniqueness the client pretends to enforce: addGuests.schema.ts has no uniqueness refinement and the handler filter only removes guests already present among booking.attendees, not duplicates within the input array, so createMany can be handed two identical emails. Additionally the attendee check is a check-then-act race: attendees are read at line 26 and written at line 92 with no transaction, so two concurrent addGuests calls (organizer + attendee, or double submit from two clients) both pass the filter and double-insert — either crashing on a unique(bookingId,email) constraint with an unhandled Prisma P2002 (the update is not wrapped in try/catch) or persisting duplicate attendee rows that produce duplicate calendar entries and duplicate emails. Dedupe the input server-side and convert constraint violations into a typed TRPCError.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The isTeamAdminOrOwner flag uses && instead of ||, so only users who are simultaneously admin and owner pass, wrongly denying plain team admins (or owners) with FORBIDDEN.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The permission flag named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` instead of `||`, so a user must be BOTH a team admin and a team owner to qualify. A plain team ADMIN who is not the owner (and, depending on isTeamAdmin's role handling, even a lone OWNER) is denied with FORBIDDEN for team bookings, contradicting the flag's name and the intended access rule.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: findFirstOrThrow on `booking.userId || 0` throws an unhandled Prisma error for any booking whose userId is null, turning the mutation into a 500 instead of a typed TRPCError.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The code guards nullable `booking.userId` with `|| 0`, but user id 0 never exists, so for any booking with a null userId (e.g. organizer account deleted, which the null-guard itself anticipates) `findFirstOrThrow` throws an unhandled PrismaClientKnownRequestError instead of a typed TRPCError — an attendee who passes the isAttendee permission check at line 52 gets a raw 500 from the mutation. Fail fast with a typed error when userId is null.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, so team admins who are not owners are wrongly denied permission to add guests.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable is named "admin OR owner" but the code requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. If isTeamAdmin matches {ADMIN, OWNER} memberships, `A && B` collapses to just isTeamOwner and plain ADMIN members are rejected with FORBIDDEN when they are neither the organizer nor an attendee; if isTeamAdmin matches only role ADMIN, the expression can never be true (a membership has a single role) and the team-permission path is entirely dead. The operator disagrees with the declared intent — replace `&&` with `||` so team admins and team owners are both permitted.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the raw input `guests` instead of the computed `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees to be resent a full booking-confirmation email.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler carefully computes `uniqueGuests` (input minus existing attendees minus blacklisted emails) at :74-78 and uses it for the DB write, but then passes the original unfiltered `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` at :168. In email-manager.ts:541, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides who gets a full AttendeeScheduledEmail ("you're booked") versus AttendeeAddGuestsEmail ("guests added"); with the raw list, any existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (or a blacklisted address that coincides) matches and receives a duplicate full booking confirmation instead of the guests-added notification. Pass `uniqueGuests`, the value that names the guests actually added.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The organizer's credentials are fetched in the booking query but never used — the EventManager is built from the requesting user, so calendar attendee updates run with the wrong user for non-organizers.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The prisma query (:35-39) includes `booking.user` with `credentials: true`, but `booking.user.credentials` is never referenced — dead data. The EventManager at :160-163 is instead constructed from `...user` (ctx.user, the requesting session user) with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` at :158. The permission gate at :54 explicitly allows non-organizers (attendees, team owners/admins) to add guests; in those cases `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` at :165 runs with the requesting user's identity and credentials rather than the booking organizer's (booking.userId), so the organizer's Google/Outlook event keeps the old attendee list. The fetched organizer credentials and the user actually used disagree — build the EventManager from the booking's organizer (booking.user) and its credentials.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback in onError can never execute because the template literal assigned to `message` is always truthy.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `message` is a template literal (`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`), which is always a non-empty, truthy string — even with both interpolations undefined it evaluates to "undefined: undefined" — so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never yields the fallback; the newly added "unable_to_add_guests" locale string is unreachable dead code. Condition on the error content instead so the fallback can actually run.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The guest filter neither dedupes the input array nor compares case-insensitively, so one request can create duplicate attendees and mixed-case emails bypass the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blocklist.
suggestions.suggestionContent: uniqueGuests (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only removes guests that exactly match an existing attendee email or a blocklist entry — it never dedupes the input array itself, and it compares raw guest strings against a list that was lowercased. The server schema (addGuests.schema.ts:5) is z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine, so the uniqueness rule exists only client-side (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29) and is bypassable by any direct mutation call. Consequences: (a) guests=["a@x.com","a@x.com"] survives the filter and createMany (handler:99-106) writes two identical Attendee rows (or surfaces a raw Prisma unique-constraint error), and that address then receives the same 'scheduled' email twice via email-manager.ts:539-547; (b) with BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS="bad@example.com", the entry is lowercased at handler:71 but the guest is compared raw at handler:77, so "BAD@example.com" is added and emailed despite being blocklisted; (c) the case-sensitive === at handler:76 lets "A@x.com" duplicate an existing "a@x.com" attendee even through the UI, since the client refine is also exact-string. Deduplicate the input with a Set of normalized emails and compare case-insensitively on both sides (and mirror the uniqueness .refine in the server schema).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw guests input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests array, so an already-attendee email is misclassified as a new guest and gets the full 'You're scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' email.
suggestions.suggestionContent: handler:168 calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the RAW input, while the DB write (handler:99-106) used uniqueGuests. When the input contains an email that is already an attendee (or was blocklisted), it is filtered out of uniqueGuests but still present in guests, so email-manager.ts:541-542 (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) classifies that existing attendee as a newly added guest and sends them AttendeeScheduledEmail — a full 'You're scheduled' confirmation as if the booking were just created — instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'New guests added' notification. Pass the array that was actually persisted (uniqueGuests) so the email-type selection matches the DB write.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Handler sends raw `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`, so already-attendee emails receive a duplicate "You're scheduled" email rather than the guests-added notification.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler passes the raw `guests` input to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, but that function's `newGuests` parameter (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541) is used to decide who is a newly added attendee: emails in `newGuests` get a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` ("You're scheduled" with a fresh ICS), everyone else gets the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification. Since only `uniqueGuests` (line 74-78) were actually added to the booking, any submitted email that is already an attendee — which the dialog's client-side validation permits, because its `.refine` only checks duplicates within the submitted array — receives a misleading "You're scheduled" email as if they just booked, instead of the "Guests Added" notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` so the producer and consumer agree on what "new guests" means.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: evt built by the handler never sets `team`, so sendAddGuestsEmails' team-member notification loop (email-manager.ts:531) can never run for team bookings.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `evt: CalendarEvent` built here never populates `team`, but the new `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531-537) — modeled on `sendLocationChangeEmails` — explicitly iterates `calendarEvent.team?.members` to send `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` to each team member. Because `evt.team` is always undefined for this caller, that branch is dead code: for team event-type bookings, team members never receive the guests-added notification. Either populate `evt.team` (name + members) for team bookings the way other booking flows do, or remove the team loop from the consumer so the two files don't disagree about whether team will be provided.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Server-side validation lacks the in-array email-uniqueness rule the dialog enforces, so a direct API call with duplicate emails creates duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The dialog's client schema (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29) refines the guest array for uniqueness, but the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (addGuests.schema.ts) has no such refine, and `uniqueGuests` here only filters emails that already exist as booking attendees — it does not dedupe duplicates WITHIN the submitted array. A direct authed tRPC call with guests=["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes validation, both copies survive the filter, `createMany` (line 101) inserts two identical attendee rows, and email-manager.ts:540 then maps over both rows sending two identical scheduled emails to the same address (or an unhandled Prisma unique-constraint error, if one exists on (bookingId, email)). Dedupe the input array (`[...new Set(guests)]`) or add the uniqueness `.refine` to `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` so the server upholds the contract the dialog assumes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google token refresh stores the zod safeParse wrapper object as the credential key, permanently breaking the integration on the next load
suggestions.suggestionContent: The value stored as the credential `key` is the zod `safeParse` WRAPPER object `{ success: true, data: {...} }` returned by `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, not the parsed credentials (previously the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`). This permanently breaks the user's Google Calendar integration after the first token refresh: on the next service instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (CalendarService.ts:75) runs against `{success: true, data: {...}}`, which lacks `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `token_type`, `expiry_date` and `scope` (all required by googleCredentialSchema.ts:3-9), so the constructor throws a ZodError for every calendar operation until the app is reinstalled. This affects the default (sharing-disabled) configuration. Fix: store the parsed data, e.g. `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;` — note the helper already throws when parsing fails, so `.data` is always defined.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Sync mode returns a raw fetch Response that axios/SDK-based callers cannot consume, crashing or corrupting token refresh for zoho-bigin, zohocrm, hubspot, google, lark and webex
suggestions.suggestionContent: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response, but the call sites expect provider-native response objects, so token refresh crashes or corrupts credentials for most integrations when sharing is enabled: zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:96 (`tokenInfo.data.error` — a fetch Response has no `.data`, so this is a TypeError crash) and zohocrm CalendarService.ts:217 crash outright; hubspot CalendarService.ts:192-198 reads `.expiresIn` from the Response (undefined → `expiryDate: NaN`), stores the Response object as the credential key (JSON-serializes to `{"expiryDate":null}`, destroying the saved tokens) and calls `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(undefined)`; google CalendarService.ts:94 (`res?.data` → undefined → `token.access_token` throws, swallowed by the catch so the refresh silently no-ops); lark CalendarService.ts:84 → handleLarkError (larkcalendar/common.ts:18) throws unless the body has `code === 0`, which the documented `{access_token, expiry}` sync body never has; webex VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 rejects because `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires refresh_token fields the sync body lacks. No single endpoint response shape can satisfy all these consumers (lark needs `{code, msg, data}`, office365/zoom expect provider JSON, axios apps need `.data`). Fix: parse the sync response once in the helper (e.g. `await response.json()`) and return a normalized object/JSON body that each app's existing validation path (its own zod schema) can consume.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes the credential row id as the sync endpoint's calcomUserId instead of the user id
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third argument passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (assigned at line 53 as `credential.id`, the credential row's primary key), but the parameter is the user id (`userId: number | null`), which the helper sends to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). When credential sharing is enabled, the parent app's sync endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credential row id>` instead of the user's id, so it resolves the wrong entity and returns the wrong user's credentials (or fails), breaking zoho-bigin token refresh for every sharing-enabled instance. Every sibling integration passes `credential.userId` (e.g. zohocrm CalendarService.ts:215, office365calendar CalendarService.ts:260). Fix: thread `credential.userId` into `refreshAccessToken` and pass it as the third argument instead of `credentialId`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Team-level app credentials can be created by any accepted team member (not just admins) via an attacker-controlled state.teamId, bypassing the admin check enforced on every sibling path
suggestions.suggestionContent: The team branch authorizes team-level credential creation with only a membership check (`members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }`), while every other team-scoped credential/install path in the codebase requires admin via `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` (apps/web/pages/api/teams/googleworkspace/callback.ts:26, apps/web/pages/api/integrations/[...args].ts:42, giphy/api/add.ts:23, jitsivideo/api/add.ts:19, huddle01video/api/add.ts:19). `state.teamId` is taken from the OAuth `state` query param (decodeOAuthState), which any logged-in user can craft, so an accepted non-admin member can start an OAuth flow with `state={"teamId":X}` and create a team-level app credential for their team without admin approval — e.g. routing team bookings through their personal third-party account. Note the `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` call at line 59 is dead code for the team path (line 30 already returned when `state.teamId` is truthy, so `state?.teamId ?? null` is always `null` there, and the helper no-ops on null), indicating the admin check was intended but never applied to the team branch. Fix: call `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId })` before the team-credential `create`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Salesforce fetches and persists a fresh access token on every instantiation but builds the connection with the stale stored token
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new code in `getClient` fetches a fresh access token and persists it to the DB (lines 96-99), but then constructs the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-fetched `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, so the refreshed token is never used by the connection that triggered the refresh. If the stored token has expired, the connection runs with an invalid token and only recovers via jsforce's internal refreshFlow after a failed API call (a second refresh round-trip). Additionally, there is no expiry check before the fetch (lines 75-84), so this refresh runs unconditionally on EVERY service instantiation — the constructor calls getClient (line 57) — adding one Salesforce HTTP call plus a credential DB write to every calendar operation (availability checks run on every booking page view), where token refresh previously happened lazily via jsforce's refreshFlow. Fix: pass the refreshed token to the connection (`accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`), or drop the eager refresh and rely on jsforce's refreshFlow with the stored refresh token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: findFirst-then-create in the credential webhook races and can create duplicate credentials for the same user+app
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook performs a check-then-act (`findFirst` at line 62, then `update`/`create` at lines 72-91) with no transaction and no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent webhook calls for the same user+app (e.g. a retry racing the original push from the parent application) both see no existing credential and both execute `create`, leaving two credentials for the same app. Subsequent syncs then `findFirst` an arbitrary one of the duplicates, so the other row keeps stale keys — the codebase elsewhere shows duplicates are a real failure mode (zoomvideo/api/callback.ts:52-71 explicitly deletes pre-existing zoom_video credentials before creating, because lookups only use findFirst). Fix: wrap the lookup and write in a prisma `$transaction` with a serializable isolation level, or add a unique constraint on (userId, appId) and use `upsert`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google CalendarService persists the Zod safeParse wrapper ({ success, data }) as the credential key, corrupting every user's Google credentials on the first token refresh.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new util, packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13-30) returns the full Zod safeParse result object `{ success, data }` — never the parsed data itself. Every other consumer in this PR (office365calendar, salesforce, zoom) accesses `.success`/`.data`, but Google assigns the return value directly to `key` and persists it. After any Google token refresh, `credential.key` becomes `{ success: true, data: { access_token, refresh_token, ... } }` instead of the token object; the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor (CalendarService.ts:75) throws, bricking the Google Calendar integration until the user reconnects. Use the `.data` field of the returned wrapper.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential DB id) where refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, so the credential-sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier for zoho-bigin users.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens`'s third parameter is the **user** id, which it forwards to the credential-sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,11), and which the webhook `/api/webhook/app-credential` later uses as the userId for `prisma.user.findUnique` and `prisma.credential.findFirst/update`. The zoho-bigin call site passes `credentialId` (the credential's DB id) instead — every other integration in this PR passes `credential.userId`. In sync mode the endpoint receives a credential id labeled as a user id, so zoho-bigin token sync silently fails or writes to the wrong user's credentials. Pass `credential.userId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but Google CalendarService reads `res?.data` (a gaxios-only shape), so Google token refresh always throws and silently keeps stale tokens.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns two different shapes: the wrapped function's return in normal mode, but a raw `fetch` Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT in sync mode (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15). Every other consumer (zoom, webex, office365video, office365calendar) calls `.json()`/`handleErrorsJson(response)` on the result — a fetch-Response shape. Google instead reads `res?.data`, which only exists on the gaxios response the non-sync path returns. When credential sharing is enabled, `res.data` is undefined, `token.access_token` throws inside the try, and the catch (CalendarService.ts:103-108) silently returns the old auth — Google tokens never refresh in the PR's own sync mode. Normalize the response (e.g. `await res.json()` when `res instanceof Response`) or have the util return a consistent shape.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Webhook secret is verified with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison on an endpoint that can overwrite any user's app credentials.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The only authentication on POST /api/webhook/app-credential is `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Ordinary string comparison short-circuits at the first differing byte, so response-time differences leak how many leading characters of the secret an attacker's guess shares; with enough probes the secret can be recovered, and knowing it grants the ability to overwrite or create ANY user's credential.key (userId and appSlug come straight from the request body, lines 31-91). Compare in constant time — hash both sides (to equalize lengths) and use crypto.timingSafeEqual — and fail when the header or the configured secret is missing.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: credential.id (the credential row PK) is passed as the user id to the credential-sync endpoint, so tokens for the wrong user can be fetched and persisted into this credential.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is documented and typed as the Cal.com user id (`userId: number | null`, refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3) and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). The Zoho Bigin adapter passes `credentialId` — `credential.id`, the Credential table primary key (CalendarService.ts:53) — instead of `credential.userId`. When credential sharing is enabled, the parent app therefore resolves the wrong identity: if the credential id collides with a different existing user's id, the sync endpoint returns THAT user's Zoho tokens, which lines 96-109 persist as this credential's key — user A's Bigin operations then run against user B's account. Without a collision the sync simply targets a non-existent user and breaks. Pass the actual user id, as every other adapter does.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The "minimum" token schema's computed keys collapse to a single constant key (only access_token is validated) and a fabricated refresh_token placeholder gets persisted, overwriting users' real refresh tokens.
suggestions.suggestionContent: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` each evaluate to a constant string (Object.prototype.toString on a zod schema object → "[object Object]"), so the two entries are the SAME key in the object literal and the second (z.unknown().optional()) silently replaces the z.number() check. The schema therefore enforces nothing the comments claim — it only requires access_token, never validates an expiry property or the token payload shape, and refresh_token is not part of it. Consequence: with sharing enabled the sync response (documented in refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7 to contain only the access token and expiry) falls through to lines 25-27, which fabricate `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`; office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 then spreads this mutated data over the existing credentials ({...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}) and persists it — the user's real refresh token is destroyed and replaced by the literal string "refresh_token". Declare the optional fields explicitly instead of computed keys, and never synthesize a fake secret value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google Calendar persists the zod safeParse wrapper object as the credential key instead of the parsed credentials, corrupting every user's Google credential after the first token refresh.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full zod safeParse result object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data. Google passes that return value straight into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so after the first token refresh the stored credential key becomes `{ success: true, data: { ... } }` instead of the credentials themselves. Before this PR the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the data). On the next load the credential no longer has top-level `access_token`/`refresh_token`/`expiry_date`, so the Google Calendar integration breaks for every user — even with credential sharing disabled, because the else-branch also uses safeParse. Note the PR's own office365calendar (`...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)`) and salesforce (`...accessTokenParsed.data`) callers unwrap `.data` correctly; Google is the odd one out. Fix: store `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The computed schema keys evaluate to the junk key "[object Object]", so under credential sharing the parse strips all fields but access_token and a literal "refresh_token" placeholder is persisted in place of the real token.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (ZodString has no toString override), and since they are identical the second silently overwrites the first. The schema actually built is `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })` — the "any property with a number is the expiry" mapping declared in the comment does not exist anywhere in the code. Because z.object strips unknown keys, under credential sharing the parse discards refresh_token, expiry_date, instance_url, etc., and lines 25-26 then inject the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" for the missing field. office365calendar spreads `tokenResponse.data` over `o365AuthCredentials`, replacing the real refresh token with the placeholder and persisting it — permanently corrupting the credential so every later refresh fails. Replace the computed keys with a real schema for the fields the endpoint actually returns (e.g. `expiry_date: z.number()`), or use a catchall/transform if the expiry key genuinely varies.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the google/hubspot/zoho callers read provider-shaped fields (.data, .refresh_token) that a fetch Response never has, so token refresh crashes for those apps.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sharing-mode branch returns the raw `fetch` Response, but several callers consume the value in the shape the offline provider client returns: googlecalendar does `const token = res?.data` and then `token.access_token` (CalendarService.ts:94-95) — a fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and the code throws a TypeError on every refresh; hubspot assigns the return to `HubspotToken` and reads token fields like `.refresh_token`/`.expires_in`; zoho-bigin and zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data.error`, which is `undefined.data` → TypeError. Only callers that pass the response through a `.json()` handler (lark, zoom, webex, office365calendar, office365video) can work with a raw Response. The wrapper should parse the endpoint's JSON (and ideally validate it) and return a shape the callers can consume — or every caller's sharing path must be adjusted — so the return type at the write site matches what each read site consumes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter, so the credential-sync endpoint receives the credential row's id as the Cal.com user id.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third argument of `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` is consumed as the Cal.com user id — under sharing mode it is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential row's id) instead of the user id; every sibling call site in this PR (googlecalendar, hubspot, lark, office365, office365video, webex, zohocrm, zoom) passes `credential.userId`. With sharing enabled the sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier and cannot resolve the user, so token sync fails or attaches tokens to the wrong identity. Pass the user id (propagate `credential.userId` into that scope as the other adapters do).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google Calendar persists the zod safeParse envelope as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential after the first token refresh.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse() returns a zod SafeParseReturnType (`{ success, data }`), but this consumer — unlike the office365, zoom and salesforce consumers — stores the return value directly as the credential key. Previously this line stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the parsed credential object). Now `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` persists `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, so after the first token refresh the stored Google credential no longer matches the GoogleCredential shape (refresh_token/expiry_date are nested under `data`) and every subsequent refresh fails. Unwrap `.data` (and re-validate with googleCredentialSchema so the injected placeholder is normalized away) before persisting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint, but Hubspot/Zoho/Google/Lark/Webex/Zoom consumers still parse provider-specific response shapes and break.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the credential-sharing branch this helper returns the raw `fetch` Response of the sync endpoint, but every caller was written against the app-specific response its `refreshFunction` produced: hubspot treats it as a HubspotToken SDK object (reads `.access_token`/`.refresh_token`), zohocrm/zoho-bigin treat it as an axios response (read `.data.error`), google reads `res?.data` (gaxios), lark/webex/o365/zoom feed it to handlers that JSON-parse a provider-shaped envelope. None of these consumers were updated for a bare fetch Response whose body is just `{ access_token, expiry }` (per the code comment). The sharing-enabled path therefore breaks every one of these refresh flows (undefined fields / TypeError on `.data`). Return a normalized parsed body (e.g. `await response.json()` with an explicit documented shape) and update each consumer to read that shape, or have the sync endpoint proxy the provider's response verbatim.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The minimum token schema's computed keys collapse to "[object Object]", so zod strips every field except access_token and then a literal "refresh_token" placeholder is injected and persisted over the real refresh token.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The "minimum" schema does not do what its comments claim: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]" (zod schemas don't override toString; the two computed keys collide), so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: z.string() }` plus an optional "[object Object]" field, and `z.object` strips every other key from the parsed output. Lines 25-27 then inject the literal string `"refresh_token"` when it is missing, and consumers persist that placeholder over the real stored token — e.g. office365calendar CalendarService.ts:263-267 spreads `tokenResponse.data` (now `{ access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token" }`) into `o365AuthCredentials` and writes it to the DB, permanently destroying the ability to refresh; zoom persists the parsed data into the credential key the same way. Use `.passthrough()` (or a real expiry field) so existing credential fields survive parsing, and do not fabricate a `refresh_token` placeholder — let each app keep its stored refresh token (as the salesforce consumer already does).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Salesforce service construction now eagerly refreshes the token and hard-fails (HttpError / schema reject) where it previously built a jsforce connection from stored credentials with lazy refresh, so any token-endpoint issue now fails every Salesforce calendar operation.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new eager refresh changes the construction contract from "build a jsforce Connection from the stored credential" (no network I/O, refresh handled lazily by jsforce) to "perform a blocking token refresh on every operation and throw on failure": `response.statusText !== "OK"` throws HttpError, and the response is validated against the new `salesforceTokenSchema`, which requires `scope` — a field Salesforce's refresh_token grant response does not reliably include (it returns access_token, signature, instance_url, id, token_type, issued_at). Any token-endpoint error, or a response missing `scope`, now rejects `this.conn` and fails every Salesforce calendar operation (booking, availability, event sync) that previously could proceed from stored credentials. Make `scope` optional in the schema (or fall back to the stored value), gate on `response.ok` rather than statusText, and consider keeping the refresh lazy/best-effort instead of failing construction.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The minimum token schema's computed keys collapse to a meaningless "[object Object]" key and z.object strips refresh_token, so lines 25-27 replace the real refresh token with the literal string "refresh_token", which callers persist and which permanently breaks OAuth integrations.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The minimum token schema is broken and corrupts stored credentials. `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]" (ZodType does not override toString), so both computed keys collide and the second (z.unknown().optional()) overwrites the intended expiry check — the schema is effectively {access_token: string, "[object Object]": optional}. Because z.object strips unknown keys, the sharing-enabled branch strips refresh_token/expiry_date/instance_url/signature from the parsed result, and lines 25-27 then assign the literal string "refresh_token" to data.refresh_token. Callers merge this into live credentials and persist it: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-268 spreads tokenResponse.data over o365AuthCredentials, replacing the real Microsoft refresh token with the literal on the very first refresh, and salesforce CalendarService.ts:96-99 stores a key stripped of instance_url/signature/id/issued_at. Declare the real key names explicitly and never substitute a placeholder for a missing refresh_token — leave it absent so callers' existing credential value survives the merge.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: refreshAccessToken stores the Zod safeParse wrapper {success, data} as the credential key instead of the parsed data, so the first Google token refresh corrupts credential.key and breaks all later GoogleCalendarService loads.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshAccessToken stores the raw return value of parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key. That function returns the whole ZodSafeParseReturnType (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 — `return refreshTokenResponse`, i.e. {success, data} / {success, error}), not the parsed data. The replaced code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` — plain data. After the first token refresh, credential.key becomes {"success":true,"data":{...}} so the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation fails its credential parse and reads googleCredentials.refresh_token === undefined — an unhandled throw and permanent breakage of Google Calendar for that user, even with credential sharing disabled. Unwrap before persisting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects the user id, so the credential-sync endpoint is keyed by the wrong id and can return another user's tokens into this credential.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is the user id that gets sent as `calcomUserId` to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14: `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but the zoho-bigin call passes `credentialId` — the credential row id — instead of `credential.userId`, unlike every other app migrated in this PR (hubspot, lark, office365calendar, office365video, webex, zoom, zohocrm all pass credential.userId). When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint is keyed by the wrong id: it either fails or returns tokens belonging to a different user, which are then written into this user's credential below (`tokenInfo.data` → prisma.credential.update) — cross-user credential corruption. Pass credential.userId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The credential-sync webhook throws unhandled ZodError/SyntaxError on body-less or malformed requests and stores unvalidated/possibly-duplicated credentials.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new webhook has three robustness/state defects. (1) There is no req.method check; a GET/HEAD with a valid secret header reaches appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) with req.body === undefined → the ZodError is unhandled → 500. (2) JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)) at :57-59 throws unhandled on malformed ciphertext or a wrong CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY — use safeParse/try-catch and return 400s. (3) `keys` is persisted into credential.key with no shape validation (a scalar/array JSON value creates a credential whose key isn't an object, breaking every later consumer that does credential.key.<field>), and the findFirst→update/create sequence is not atomic: two concurrent sync calls for the same (userId, appId) can both pass findFirst(null) and both create, leaving duplicate credentials. Validate the decrypted value is an object and make the read-modify-write atomic (e.g. interactive transaction or upsert on a unique (userId, appId) constraint).

suggestions.label: bug
