suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes the credential row ID into refreshOAuthTokens' `userId` position, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential ID as `calcomUserId`.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third parameter of refreshOAuthTokens (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3) is the Cal.com user ID, and when credential sharing is enabled it is sent as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10-13). zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` there, which is `credential.id` (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:53) — the credential row's primary key, not the user's ID. In sharing mode the parent app then resolves a user by that wrong number: either an unknown user (refresh fails, Bigin integration breaks) or a *different* user whose id happens to equal the credential id, whose tokens are then persisted into this user's credential (lines 102-109). Every other call site in this PR passes `credential.userId` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:92, office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:74, office365calendar:260, hubspot:188, lark:81, webex:77, zohocrm:215, zoomvideo:93) — zoho-bigin is the outlier. Pass the user id from the credential instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The zod safeParse envelope `{success, data}` is stored as the Google credential key, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and Google Calendar breaks after the first token refresh.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole zod safeParse result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed value — unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` call this line replaced. Line 97 binds that envelope to `key` and lines 98-101 persist it as `credential.key`. On the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation, line 75 runs `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` against `{success: true, data: {...}}`, which has no top-level access_token/refresh_token — the parse throws (or, under a lenient schema, yields an empty object), so the Google Calendar service is unusable for that user. This hits the default path too: with credential sharing disabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:18 takes the `schema.safeParse` branch and still returns the envelope. office365calendar shows the intended usage — it destructures `.data` explicitly (`...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` both evaluate to `"[object Object]"`, so the minimum token schema silently validates/passes only `access_token` and strips the expiry field it is documented to accept.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate identically: `z.string()` creates a ZodString instance with no custom `toString`, so `.toString()` returns Object.prototype.toString's `"[object Object]"`. The object literal therefore has two duplicate `"[object Object]"` keys and the second (`z.unknown().optional()`) overwrites the first — the schema compiles to `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`. The comments' assumptions ("any property with a number is the expiry", "allow other properties") never match a single real property: in sharing mode the parent's response is safeParsed with this schema (line 16), so only `access_token` survives zod's default stripping. The expiry the sync endpoint is documented to return (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7: "should only contain the access token and expiry date") is dropped from `data`, so consumers like office365calendar (which spreads `tokenResponse.data` over its credentials) never receive an updated expiry, and `refresh_token` is always missing (feeding the placeholder bug at lines 25-27). Define the expiry fields explicitly and use `.passthrough()` if other properties must be kept.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The truthiness check `!data.refresh_token` unconditionally injects the literal string "refresh_token" into parsed token data, and callers like office365calendar then persist that junk literal over the user's real refresh token.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 25 tests for absence using truthiness and, whenever the validated data has no `refresh_token`, writes the literal string `"refresh_token"` into it — regardless of whether credential sharing is actually active (the branch at lines 15-19 only selects the schema). This placeholder is only meaningful when the parent app owns the refresh flow, yet it is applied on the default non-sharing path too. Concrete corruption: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-267 builds `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` and persists that object — the placeholder (guaranteed present in sharing mode because the `"[object Object]"` schema strips the field, and possible in non-sharing mode for any provider/schema that omits refresh_token, e.g. the new salesforceTokenSchema) overwrites the real refresh token held in `o365AuthCredentials`. If credential sharing is later disabled, the next refresh posts `refresh_token="refresh_token"` to login.microsoftonline.com, gets invalid_grant, and the user's calendar is permanently disconnected. Salesforce only escapes because its object literal places `refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token` after the spread. Guard the placeholder to the sharing branch (and prefer preserving an existing refresh token at the call site).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Retry counter permanently deletes pending SMS reminders after 2 cron runs for temporarily locked/rate-limited accounts (and during transient outages), silently dropping reminders that would previously have been retried until scheduledDate.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new retry counter treats temporary, account-level failures the same as permanent per-reminder failures — twilio.scheduleSMS returns undefined (falsy) whenever the user/team is in SMSLockState.LOCKED (twilioProvider.ts:92-95), and hitting the else branch increments retryCount, after which the new deleteMany branch (lines 38-42) permanently deletes the reminder once retryCount > 1. WHY: checkSMSRateLimit does not throw — it sets SMSLockState.LOCKED when the monthly SMS quota is exceeded (checkRateLimitAndThrowError.ts:40-45). A user/team over quota gets every pending unscheduled SMS reminder deleted after just 2 consecutive cron runs (retryCount 0→1→2, then deleteMany on the next run), before scheduledDate is even near. When the lock clears (quota reset next month, admin unlock), the reminders are gone and those workflow SMS messages are silently never sent. The same 2-strike mass deletion applies to transient Twilio API outages and transient DB/parse errors caught at line 189 — previously these reminders were retried until scheduledDate passed, giving up to 7 days for conditions to clear. HOW: Only count reminder-specific/permanent failures (e.g., Twilio invalid-number errors) toward retryCount, or skip incrementing when isLockedForSMSSending is the cause (e.g., have scheduleSMS distinguish 'locked' from 'failed'), or raise the retry budget / delete only when scheduledDate is imminent so temporary conditions can recover.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Catch block counts post-success prisma update failures and unrelated transient errors toward retryCount, so a reminder with a live scheduled Twilio SMS can be deleted from the DB, making the SMS uncancellable.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The catch block increments retryCount for ANY exception thrown anywhere in the try block — including the prisma.workflowReminder.update at lines 169-177 that runs AFTER twilio.scheduleSMS already succeeded, and unrelated transient errors (bookingMetadataSchema.parse at line 134, prisma.profile.findFirst, getBookerBaseUrl). WHY: If the post-schedule prisma update fails, the reminder stays scheduled=false with retryCount climbing while a live scheduled SMS exists in Twilio; after 2 such failures the new deleteMany branch (lines 38-42) deletes the row — and because that branch has no method:SMS scope and no scheduled:false filter (the line-28 comment says the delete is scoped to SMS), a row with a live Twilio message is destroyed, leaving an SMS that cancelWorkflowReminders can no longer cancel (it needs the row's referenceId), so customers can receive reminder SMS for cancelled bookings; intermediate runs also re-schedule and double-book the SMS. HOW: Narrow the counted try to the twilio.scheduleSMS call (or use a nested try/catch) so post-success DB update failures do not increment retryCount, and scope the deleteMany OR branch with method: WorkflowMethods.SMS (and ideally scheduled: false) to match the stated intent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: New unguarded prisma update calls in the else/catch failure paths can throw (e.g. P2025 when the reminder row is deleted by a concurrent booking cancellation/reschedule), escaping the loop and aborting the entire SMS scheduling batch where the previous catch-only-log contract guaranteed every reminder was processed and a 200 returned.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new failure-path retryCount writes broke the loop's error-containment contract. Before this PR the catch block was infallible (console.log only): a per-reminder failure — Twilio returning falsy (else branch) or throwing (catch) — was fully contained, the loop processed every remaining reminder, and the endpoint always returned 200. Now both failure paths await prisma.workflowReminder.update by id with no guard. Prisma's update throws P2025 when the row no longer exists, which is a real race (a booking cancelled/rescheduled between the findMany and this write removes its workflowReminder rows) besides transient DB errors. An exception thrown inside the catch block escapes the try/catch and the for-loop entirely: all remaining reminders in the batch are skipped this run and the cron request fails. Worse, if the else-branch update (line 179) throws, control falls into the catch which retries the identical failing update unguarded — a guaranteed second throw that aborts the whole run. Use updateMany (which does not throw on zero matches) or wrap the write in its own try/catch so retry bookkeeping can never abort the batch.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: A crafted login request with a junk totpCode plus a valid backup code bypasses password verification entirely and grants a session on the second factor alone.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new backup-code branch in authorize() can return an authenticated user without ever verifying their password: the password check at next-auth-options.ts:121 (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`) is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is non-empty, and the new branch at :131 (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`) validates only the backup code. A direct POST to /api/auth/callback/credentials with any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "1"), any junk `password`, and a valid `backupCode` therefore grants a full session using only the second factor — an attacker who obtains the victim's cal-backup-codes.txt (the plaintext file this PR tells users to download) logs in without knowing the password. The sibling endpoint disable.ts:40-45 always verifies the password before the backup-code check, confirming the intended contract is password + backup code; the web UI is safe only because it clears totpCode in lost-access mode. Fix by verifying the password for CAL users before the backup-code branch regardless of totpCode (mirror disable.ts). Note also that the backup code is consumed/persisted at :148-156 before the rest of authorize() completes, so any later throw burns the code without granting a session.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: After enabling 2FA, closing the backup-codes dialog via X or Escape skips onEnable(), leaving the settings switch showing 2FA as disabled.
suggestions.suggestionContent: handleEnable no longer calls onEnable() when the enable request succeeds — line 135 replaced it with `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)`, and onEnable() now fires only from the backup-codes "close" button (lines 263-272). On the DisplayBackupCodes step the cancel button is hidden (line 222), so a user who dismisses the dialog with the header X button or the Escape key never triggers onEnable(). The parent (apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:62-72) only invalidates the `viewer.me` cache inside onEnable (onOpenChange at :64 just flips the open flag), so the 2FA switch keeps rendering the stale unchecked state even though 2FA is now enabled server-side; clicking the switch again reopens the setup wizard and the setup endpoint returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled, surfacing "something_went_wrong". Pre-PR, onEnable() fired immediately on the 200 response so this stale state could not occur. Fix by invalidating viewer.me in the parent's onOpenChange (or splitting close vs. invalidate) so every dismissal path refreshes the switch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Existing 2FA users who lose their authenticator hit a dead-end error telling them to regenerate backup codes in settings, which is impossible from the login screen and unsupported by any endpoint.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new MissingBackupCodes handling dead-ends users with an impossible instruction. The migration adds `backupCodes` as NULL with no backfill, so every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy has `backupCodes = null` while `twoFactorEnabled = true`; setup.ts:42-44 rejects regeneration for already-enabled accounts (TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled), and no other endpoint in this PR regenerates codes. When such a user loses their authenticator and uses the "Lost access" flow, next-auth-options.ts:137 throws MissingBackupCodes and login.tsx:158 shows "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." — but they cannot reach settings (they are locked out, that's why they're using the backup path) and even a logged-in user has no regeneration action; their only recovery is fully disabling and re-enabling 2FA. Either backfill/generate backup codes for existing twoFactorEnabled users (e.g. on demand at first use, or a regenerate action in security settings) or reword the message to describe the actual recovery path.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup-code verification on the login path uses non-constant-time indexOf, leaking match-length information about a secret credential.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new backup-code verification compares a secret authentication credential with `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`. `indexOf` uses ordinary `===`, which short-circuits on the first differing character, so per-request timing can in principle leak how many leading characters of a stored backup code are correct — exactly the property constant-time comparison exists to prevent. Codes are fixed 10-character hex strings, so `crypto.timingSafeEqual` is directly applicable (add `import crypto from "crypto"` if not present). Practical exploitability is limited (the branch runs only after a correct password and network jitter is large), hence medium severity, but the fix is cheap and the class requires constant-time comparison of credentials.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The disable-2FA endpoint verifies backup codes with non-constant-time indexOf, leaking match-length information about a stored credential.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same defect as the login path, one endpoint over: the new branch added in this PR verifies the submitted backup code with `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` (line 61). `indexOf` is an ordinary short-circuiting `===` comparison of a secret credential and is not constant-time; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (codes are fixed 10-char hex, so equal-length buffers are guaranteed after a length guard). Also note `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws a TypeError when a client sends a non-string value, turning a bad request into a 500 — coercing with String(...) fixes both.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The backup-code component is declared as `TwoFactor`, contradicting its file name (BackupCode.tsx), every import (`BackupCode`), and what it renders.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new component in BackupCode.tsx is exported as `function TwoFactor({ center = true })`, but the file is BackupCode.tsx, it registers the `backupCode` form field and renders a backup-code TextField, and every import site names it `BackupCode` (login.tsx:32, DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8). The identifier `TwoFactor` states the opposite of what this code is — a copy-paste leftover from TwoFactor.tsx. In DevTools, stack traces, and greps for `TwoFactor`, this backup-code component appears under the TOTP component's name, misleading maintainers. Rename it to match the file and its usage.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The disable endpoint's log message says "backup code login" but this handler disables 2FA, not logs a user in.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new branch in the 2FA *disable* endpoint logs `console.error("Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login.")` when CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing. This handler is POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable (an authenticated user disabling 2FA), not a login flow; the message was copy-pasted from next-auth-options.ts:133 where "login" is accurate. An operator triaging a missing-encryption-key incident on this endpoint is told the wrong operation was rejected. Align the message with what the endpoint does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new missing-backup-codes message tells users to "generate them in your settings", which is impossible at the login screen where the message is displayed and does not exist as a feature anywhere in this PR.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new `missing_backup_codes` string — "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." — is rendered in the login flow (login.tsx:158, driven by the throw at next-auth-options.ts:137) and in the disable-2FA modal (DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:75-76). In both contexts the instruction is untrue: at the login screen the user cannot reach settings without logging in (exactly what they are failing to do), and this PR adds no way to generate backup codes from settings — they are only created during the enable flow (setup.ts:61) and are nulled on disable (disable.ts:107). Every pre-existing 2FA user (the migration leaves `backupCodes` NULL) who clicks "Lost access" hits this dead-end message. Reword to something accurate and actionable for both contexts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The enable-2FA step's switch assertion is vacuous (a Promise is always truthy), and this PR's new backup-codes step means the switch is genuinely unchecked at that point, so the test passes only because the assertion verifies nothing.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This PR adds a FIXME admitting the assertion is vacuous but leaves it in place: `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` can never fail because the `await` binds to `expect()`, so `toBeTruthy()` receives the Promise object from `isChecked()`, which is always truthy. Worse, this PR's new DisplayBackupCodes step (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx now calls `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of `onEnable()` after a successful enable) means the switch is never actually checked at this point in the first test — the dialog is never closed, so `onEnable()` never fires. The assertion therefore names a state that is now false and still passes. Fix the test like the second test does: click `backup-codes-close` after fillOtp, then assert the checked state.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The copy-button test asserts only a toast that the handler shows unconditionally (clipboard writeText is never awaited), so it passes even when the copy fails or copies empty/wrong text.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new copy-button test's only assertion is that the toast appears, but the handler it covers (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx copy button) calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without awaiting it and then unconditionally shows the success toast. The test therefore passes even if writeText is removed, rejects (as it can in headless browsers without clipboard permissions), or copies an empty/incorrect string. Grant clipboard permissions and assert the clipboard contents equal the formatted backup codes (and consider awaiting writeText in the handler so the toast reflects actual success).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new backup-codes block never asserts any actual code value — grid contents, downloaded file contents, or clipboard text — so a regression generating zero or malformed backup codes would still pass.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new block's premise is "backup codes are now showing", yet nothing asserts a single code value anywhere: the download check asserts only suggestedFilename (which comes from the `download` attribute and is identical for an empty file), and the grid of codes is rendered but never asserted. If setup.ts generated an empty array or garbage codes, the blob URL is still created, the download event still fires with the right filename, and the test stays green. Assert the downloaded file contains 10 lines in the expected XXXXX-XXXXX hex format (or assert the grid renders 10 matching entries).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex but both case-sensitive indexOf validators reject a correctly typed uppercase-hex code, breaking the lost-access recovery path.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Generator and validator disagree on case. setup.ts (this PR) generates backup codes with `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, i.e. lowercase hex, and EnableTwoFactorModal displays/copies/downloads them as lowercase. But this hunk validates the user-supplied code with a case-sensitive `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` — `indexOf` is a strict `===`. The new BackupCode.tsx input does not normalize case and its placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX" actively suggests uppercase; a user who retypes a valid code using uppercase hex letters (about 90% of codes contain a–f) gets ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode and is told the code is wrong — on the "lost access" recovery path where the user has no other way in. The identical case-sensitive comparison exists in the sibling consumer added by this PR, apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 (`backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`). Normalize the input at both comparison sites, e.g. `backupCodes.indexOf(String(credentials.backupCode).replaceAll("-", "").toLowerCase())` (and likewise for `req.body.backupCode` in disable.ts), or normalize case consistently when generating and comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new BackupCode component's default-export function is copy-pasted as `TwoFactor`, mislabeling it in DevTools, error stacks, and maintainers' greps.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new component in BackupCode.tsx is declared as `export default function TwoFactor(...)` — a copy-paste leftover from duplicating TwoFactor.tsx. It is functionally harmless (default exports are renamed on import, so `import BackupCode from "@components/auth/BackupCode"` works), but the component will show up as "TwoFactor" in React DevTools, profiler traces and error stacks even though it renders the backup-code field, and maintainers grepping for `function TwoFactor` will now find two unrelated components. Rename the declaration to `BackupCode` to match the file, the import sites in login.tsx:32 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8, and the field it registers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The login page's backupCode never reaches the credentials provider — the unchanged zod formSchema strips it and the unchanged nextAuth.signIn call doesn't forward it — so "lost access" login always loops on SecondFactorRequired and the newly added IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes branches are unreachable dead code.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The PR wires `backupCode` at both ends but not in the middle. BackupCode.tsx:25 registers "backupCode" in the form and next-auth-options.ts:131/137-145 reads `credentials.backupCode`, but nothing carries the value across: (1) the form submits through `zodResolver(formSchema)` (login.tsx:67) and zod strips keys absent from the schema — this PR adds `backupCode` only to the `LoginValues` TypeScript interface (line 43), never to `formSchema`; (2) the `nextAuth.signIn("credentials", ...)` call is not modified by any hunk in this PR, so it cannot forward the new field. Result: a user who clicks "Lost access", types a valid backup code and submits gets `SecondFactorRequired` again forever (totpCode was cleared at login.tsx:109-125), the new error branches at lines 157-158 (`IncorrectBackupCode`, `MissingBackupCodes`) are unreachable dead code, and users who lost their authenticator are locked out despite holding valid backup codes. Fix: add `backupCode` to the zod formSchema and pass it through the `nextAuth.signIn` call (destructure it in the submit handler and include it in the credentials payload). I could not read login.tsx directly before the step limit; if the schema already uses passthrough AND the signIn call already spreads all values, disregard — but no hunk in this PR touches either site.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: disable.ts's new backup-code branch reads user.backupCodes, but the PR never updates the endpoint's user query — if that query uses a restrictive select, every backup-code disable returns MissingBackupCodes even when codes exist.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new backup-code branch reads `user.backupCodes` at disable.ts:54 and :58, but no hunk in this PR shows the user query (lines ~30-42, above the changed region) being updated to select the new column. The same PR had to add `backupCodes: true` to the prisma select in next-auth-options.ts (line 89) for its new backup logic — evidence that selects in this codebase are restrictive and must be extended. If disable.ts's `findUnique`/`findFirst` uses a `select` that doesn't include `backupCodes`, then `user.backupCodes` is `undefined` for every request, line 54's guard always trips, and every attempt to disable 2FA via "Lost access" returns `MissingBackupCodes` ("No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.") even when the user has valid stored codes — the whole lost-access disable flow would be dead with a misleading error. Please verify the query and add `backupCodes: true` to its select (or confirm it fetches the full row). I could not read lines 1-42 of this file before the step limit, hence the flagged confidence.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Reduce-built nested Prisma.Sql objects can never structurally equal the flat single-template Prisma.sql expectations, so the team-scope, org-scope and combined-filter tests fail.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The rewritten expectations compare a flat single-template `Prisma.sql` object against conditions that the service builds by nesting `Prisma.Sql` fragments inside `Prisma.sql` templates via `conditions.reduce(...)` (insightsBooking.ts:119-122 for filters, 171-174 for org, 204-207 for team), so the compared objects are structurally different even when the rendered SQL is identical. WHY: `Prisma.sql`'s constructor stores `strings` and `values` as given — a nested fragment stays an entry inside the outer `values` array with wrapper string segments like `['(', ') OR (', ')']`, and flattening to final SQL/parameters only happens inside the query engine at execution time; since vitest `toEqual` deep-compares the own `strings`/`values` properties rather than the rendered SQL, the expected object (4 string segments, values `[teamId, [userId]]`) can never equal the produced object (strings `['(', ') OR (', ')']`, values `[Sql, Sql]`) — the "should build team scope conditions" (295-299), "should build org scope conditions" (332-343), and "should combine multiple filter conditions" (429-431) tests fail deterministically regardless of test data. (Note: single-level expectations such as lines 210, 245, 273, 384-386 and 407 do match exactly, which isolates the failure to the reduce-nested cases.) HOW: Assert on the flattened form — compare `conditions.text`/`conditions.query` (rendered SQL + flat bound values) — or normalize both sides through a helper that renders `Sql` to text+values before comparing; alternatively make the service return eagerly-flattened SQL (manual concatenation instead of reduce-wrapping) so the compared structures are canonical.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Dangling `if` in `<%- end if %>` makes the embed template a Ruby syntax error, 500ing every successful embed render.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: best.html.erb line 6 closes the header's `if/else` block with `<%- end if %>` — a dangling `if` modifier with no condition, which ERB compiles to invalid Ruby (`end if;`). WHY: ActionView raises a SyntaxError when compiling the template, so every /embed/best request that finds a topic (the main success path once an article is imported) returns a 500 instead of the comment list — the embed feature is broken in production; the controller specs don't render views, so the suite passes unnoticed. HOW: replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Embed stylesheet requires a non-existent ./vendor/normalize asset, breaking every embed page and asset precompilation.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: embed.css.scss line 1 has `//= require ./vendor/normalize`, but no vendor/ directory or normalize asset exists anywhere under app/assets/stylesheets (or the repo — verified with repo-wide glob searches); `./` makes the require strictly relative to the manifest, so it cannot resolve. WHY: compiling the 'embed' stylesheet raises Sprockets::FileNotFound; layouts/embed.html.erb renders `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, so every embed response (loading and best) errors in development and `rake assets:precompile` fails in production deploys. HOW: add the actual normalize asset at the required path, or drop the `//= require ./vendor/normalize` directive (the `./common/foundation/base` directive resolves fine).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Imported articles are stored as unsanitized raw HTML with unescaped URL interpolation, enabling stored XSS from feed/page content.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import stores external content with cook_method raw_html (which makes Post#cook at app/models/post.rb:133 return `raw` verbatim, bypassing the markdown/sanitizer pipeline) and interpolates the unescaped `url` into an HTML attribute in the "Imported from" footer: `"#{url}"`. WHY: the embed_url is validated only for scheme (/^https?/ at topic_embed.rb:11) and host (topic_retriever.rb:15), so a URL on the embeddable host whose path contains `'>` is fetched via import_remote and its URL injected raw into the stored post — and poll_feed.rb:35-36 passes RSS `content` straight through with no tag whitelist (unlike import_remote's readability `tags:` restriction) — so external feed/page HTML is rendered unsanitized via `raw post.cooked` (best.html.erb:19) to every viewer: a stored XSS on the Discourse origin. HOW: HTML-escape the URL when building the imported_from footer (ERB::Util.h) and sanitize imported HTML through a whitelist (e.g. the sanitize gem or the same readability tag list) before storing with cook_method raw_html.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: PollFeed assumes every feed item has a content tag; one item without it crashes the whole import run with retry disabled.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: poll_feed.rb line 35 calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally, but simple-rss does not produce a value for feed items that lack `<content>`/`<content:encoded>` — plain RSS 2.0 feeds (title/link/description only) yield nil (or raise NoMethodError in simple-rss 1.3.1's method_missing). WHY: `nil.scrub` / `CGI.unescapeHTML(nil)` raise inside the `rss.items.each` loop with no rescue and `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single such item aborts the entire hourly poll — no feed items (including valid ones after the bad item) are ever imported, and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve's synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` also dies before falling back to fetch_http. HOW: fall back to description/summary, e.g. `CGI.unescapeHTML((i.content || i.description || '').to_s.scrub)`, or rescue per item.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: absolutize_urls turns protocol-relative URLs (//host/…) into broken same-host paths.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: absolutize_urls (topic_embed.rb:62-73) treats any href/src starting with `/` as a same-site relative path, so protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` also match, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips BOTH leading slashes before re-prefixing — producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`. WHY: protocol-relative asset/link URLs are common in RSS/imported HTML, and this rewrite silently breaks those images and links (they now point at nonexistent paths on the embeddable host). HOW: only rewrite when there is exactly one leading slash (e.g. `href =~ /\A\/[^\/]/` or `href.start_with?('/') && !href.start_with?('//')`), leaving `//host/...` untouched.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The 30-second loading reload re-requests /embed/best with the iframe's own URL as referer, which fails the referer-host check and shows a 403 instead of comments.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: loading.html.erb retries via `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds, but on a frame reload the browser re-requests /embed/best with the Referer of the iframe's own Discourse URL (or no referer at all), which fails `ensure_embeddable`'s check that `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (embed_controller.rb:26). WHY: first-time visitors see "Loading Discussion..." and then a 403 "invalid access" error page inside the embed area — the retrieved comments never appear through this retry path, only after a full reload of the host page. HOW: make the retry re-supply a valid referer (e.g. have the host-page embed script re-create/navigate the iframe, or have the loading view postMessage the parent asking it to re-request), rather than reloading the frame directly.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The translated 'Imported from' footer builds its link by interpolating an unescaped external URL, which reaches the user as raw HTML.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `embed.imported_from` translation is populated with `link: "#{url}"` built by raw string interpolation. `url` is external input (an RSS ``/`` via poll_feed.rb:32-33, or a request-supplied embed_url) that is only checked to start with `http(s)://`; single quotes and parentheses are valid URI path characters, so neither the regex at line 11 nor `URI(url)` in absolutize_urls rejects them. Because the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html` (Post#cook returns the raw string untouched, app/models/post.rb:133) and the view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), nothing escapes this message on its way to the user: a URL containing `'` breaks out of the single-quoted href attribute and injects arbitrary attributes/markup into the page shown to readers. HTML-escape the URL when building the link (and use an `_html`-suffixed key so the HTML intent is explicit), so the user always sees a well-formed link rather than attacker-controlled HTML.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Embedded comment dates use a hard-coded English strftime format instead of the site's translation mechanism.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `post.created_at.strftime("%e %b %Y")` hard-codes an English-locale date format (`%b` renders English month abbreviations) in a user-facing view, while every other user-visible string in the same template goes through I18n (`I18n.t('embed.title')` line 3, `I18n.t('embed.start_discussion')` line 5, `I18n.t('embed.continue')` line 25). On a Discourse instance running any other locale, the embedded comments will still read "10 Feb 2013" with English month names. Format the date with the localized helper (e.g. `I18n.l`) so the display follows the site locale like the neighbouring strings.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The validated referer is echoed unescaped into a JavaScript string literal in the served embed page.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` interpolates the raw Referer header into a JavaScript string literal in the HTML sent to the user. The `ensure_embeddable` filter (embed_controller.rb:26) only compares the referer's *host* to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; its path is unvalidated, and `'`, `(`, `)` are legal URI path characters, so a referer such as `http://<embeddable-host>/x'-<injection>-'` breaks out of the JS string and injects script into the page served from the Discourse origin. Escape the value for a JavaScript context (e.g. the `j`/`to_json` helper) before embedding it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Each "requires X" test in poll_feed_spec passes even when its named guard is deleted from Jobs::PollFeed#execute, because the other two guard settings are blank by default.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The three "requires X" tests do not verify the guards they name. Jobs::PollFeed#execute (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:14-18) is a 3-condition && chain; each test stubs only ONE setting to an invalid value while leaving the other two at their site_settings.yml defaults (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: ''). Because the chain short-circuits at the unstubbed blank settings, poll_feed is never called no matter what the stubbed setting is. Consequently: if the `feed_polling_enabled?` check were deleted from execute, the "requires feed_polling_enabled?" test still passes (url/username default blank); the same holds for the feed_polling_url and embed_by_username tests. No single guard is regression-tested. Fix: in each "requires X" test, stub the other two settings to valid values (enabled true, url set, username set) so the only false condition is the one under test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: "is 404 without an embed_url" never reaches params.require — ensure_embeddable raises first because embeddable_host is blank, so it passes even with the required-param check removed.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" never exercises params.require(:embed_url). EmbedController declares `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:4), which runs before the action; in this example SiteSetting.embeddable_host is not stubbed, so it is blank (default '') and ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess at line 25 — the response is non-success before `best` (and its `params.require(:embed_url)` at line 9) is ever reached. Falsification: delete `params.require(:embed_url)` from the action entirely and this test still passes, because the non-success status comes from the host filter, not the missing parameter. It also asserts only `should_not be_success`, so the claimed "404" status is never actually checked. Fix: stub embeddable_host to a valid host and the request referer so ensure_embeddable passes, then omit embed_url and assert the actual status.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The rewired Disqus import changed the command's behaviour contract without following through. The old path (`PostCreator.new(user, title: t[:title], raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]", created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)`) worked entirely from the local Disqus XML: it never touched the network, could not fail on a missing page, and preserved each thread's original `created_at`. The replacement `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` fetches every link over HTTP (`open(url).read` in topic_embed.rb:48): when a thread's link no longer resolves — the common case when migrating an old blog's archives — open-uri raises and the exception propagates through import_remote/import, aborting the whole import mid-run with no rescue (leaving a half-migrated site and no way to resume past the bad link). Even when the fetch succeeds, `created_at` is no longer forwarded, so every imported topic is dated "today" and loses its original timestamp (and the category option was dropped). Rescue per-item errors (e.g. `rescue OpenURI::HTTPError => e; puts "skipping #{t[:link]}: #{e}"; next`) and pass a `created_at` through `TopicEmbed.import`/`PostCreator` so the previous offline, best-effort, timestamp-preserving guarantees are kept.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The ERB chunk `end if` compiles to invalid Ruby (unbalanced/unconditioned if), so embed/best raises a template SyntaxError and 500s on every request that has a topic.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 6 ends the if/else with `end if`, which is not valid Ruby in an ERB code chunk: the `end` closes the if/else from lines 2-5, and the remaining bare `if` has no condition. Counting blocks confirms it can never parse: four openers (if line 2, stray if line 6, if line 11, `each` line 12) versus only three `end` tokens (lines 6, 22, 29). Whichever way the ERB engine emits the chunk (`end if;` or `end if\n`), the compiled template raises a SyntaxError at render time, so every request to `embed/best` that finds an existing TopicEmbed returns a 500 — the primary display path of the new embedding feature never works. The controller specs stub TopicView and don't render views, so CI stays green. Replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>` (and add an integration test that renders the template).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: poll_feed calls i.content.scrub on every feed item without a guard, so a feed whose items lack a content element (or a Ruby without String#scrub) crashes the entire hourly import loop with NoMethodError and never imports the remaining items.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a content element. RSS 2.0 feeds (the most common format) carry only link/description in items, so SimpleRSS resolves `i.content` through method_missing (nil or NoMethodError) → `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole items loop. The job also sets `retry: false`, so the import dies at the first short item and every item after it is silently never imported (the job will fail at the same point every hour). Additionally, `String#scrub` only exists on Ruby >= 2.1, which postdates this code, so on the supported Ruby versions the call can raise NoMethodError even when content exists; a nil `i.title` similarly flows into PostCreator with `skip_validations: true` and produces a null-title insert failure. Guard each item (e.g. `next unless i.content.present?`) and normalize with `i.content.to_s.scrub`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: setnx and expire are separate round trips, so a crash or Redis error between them leaves the retrieved: key with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed_url and preventing it from ever being imported.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The throttle is written as two separate Redis commands: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the `retrieved:<embed_url>` key is stored with no TTL and permanently reports "retrieved recently" — perform_retrieve never runs again for that URL (Sidekiq's retry of the failed job also bails on the orphan key), so the embed is never imported and the loading view loops forever. Use a single atomic write, e.g. `$redis.set(retrieved_key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)` (or setnx+expire guarded so a failed expire deletes the key).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Deleting an imported topic leaves its topic_embeds row behind (no FK or dependent hook), which permanently 404s/raises the embed and blocks re-import because perform_retrieve bails on the stale row.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Nothing cleans up topic_embeds rows when their topic/post is destroyed (no FK in the migration, no dependent/after_destroy hook), so deleting an imported topic leaves a stale embed row. Every subsequent request for that embed_url then takes the `topic_id` branch, TopicView.new gets a nonexistent topic and raises Discourse::NotFound, and the URL can never recover: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve bails at its `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...).exists?` check, so the article is never re-imported; a later feed update for the same URL would likewise hit `PostRevisor.new(embed.post)` with embed.post nil → NoMethodError. Either destroy the TopicEmbed row when the topic/post is destroyed, or verify the topic still exists before rendering (falling back to the retrieve/loading path when it doesn't).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: absolutize_urls only converts URLs starting with '/', so relative URLs like 'hello.html' or 'images/x.jpg' are left relative and later resolve against the Discourse origin in the embed iframe.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The absolutize_urls boundary is drawn with `start_with?('/')`, which only catches root-relative URLs, while the comment ("Convert any relative URLs to absolute") and the feature's purpose cover all relative URLs. Relative hrefs/srcs without a leading slash ('hello.html', '../img/x') are stored verbatim in the raw-HTML post and, when rendered inside the Discourse iframe (best.html.erb:19), resolve against the Discourse host rather than the source article — broken images and links that point into the forum. Resolve values against the article URL itself (URI.join) instead of testing for a leading '/', and when deciding whether the port is the default, compare against the URL's own scheme default rather than a fixed 80/443 pair (line 59 drops the port for http-on-443 / https-on-80 URLs).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: embed.js concatenates discourseUrl assuming a trailing slash and validates messages by substring containment, so a discourseUrl without the slash (or protocol-relative) silently kills the iframe or the resize handling.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The script assumes discourseUrl ends with '/' when building the iframe src (line 7: raw concatenation, so "http://forum.example.com" yields the malformed src "http://forum.example.comembed/best?..." and the widget silently 404s), and separately validates postMessage senders by checking that e.origin appears anywhere inside discourseUrl (line 17), which silently drops all resize messages when discourseUrl is protocol-relative ("//forum.example.com/") even though the iframe itself loads fine. Normalize the value once up front (ensure the trailing slash, require an absolute http(s) URL) and compare the sender against the extracted origin instead of substring containment.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The embed layout reflects the raw Referer header into an inline JS string without JS-string escaping, allowing script injection into the response on the Discourse origin.
suggestions.suggestionContent: request.referer (a fully client-controlled header) is echoed into the response inside a single-quoted JavaScript string. Rails' <%= %> html escaping does not escape single quotes on Rails 3.2.12 (this app's Gemfile.lock pins rails 3.2.12), so a Referer such as http://<embeddable_host>/?q=';attacker-code;// — which passes the host check in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable (URI allows ' in query strings) — breaks out of the string and executes attacker script inside the embed iframe, which runs on the Discourse origin (session cookie / private data reachable by the script). The postMessage payload is only the page height, so the referer does not need to be echoed at all: post to '*', or at minimum json-escape the value. Reported because attacker-controlled request data leaves in the response in an executable context.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: TopicEmbed.import interpolates the unescaped URL into post HTML that is stored unsanitized (raw_html cook method) and rendered with raw, so external feed/embed content leaves in responses as live HTML.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 13 builds the 'imported from' footer by raw string interpolation of url into HTML (#{url}), and that markup ends up in the post body verbatim: the new cook_method raw_html in Post#cook (app/models/post.rb:133) makes cooked == raw with no sanitization, and the embed view renders it with <%= raw post.cooked %> (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19) while the ordinary topic view renders cooked as HTML as well. The url originates from externally controlled data — RSS item link/id in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32-33, or the embed_url request param flowing EmbedController#best -> Jobs::RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever#fetch_http -> import_remote — and poll_feed.rb:35 further entity-decodes feed content via CGI.unescapeHTML, turning even escaped HTML into live tags. Escape the URL when building the footer (single quotes are legal in URIs, so href-attribute breakout remains possible even though URI.parse inside absolutize_urls blocks '<' and whitespace in the url), and sanitize imported content before storing it as raw HTML.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new embedding site settings are written as scalar values instead of the nested `default:` attribute hashes used by every other entry in this file, so the settings consumed by embed_controller.rb, poll_feed.rb and topic_retriever.rb are never registered with valid defaults/types and the embedding feature cannot work.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
The new `embedding:` settings block is written as bare scalars (`embeddable_host: ''`, `feed_polling_enabled: false`, `feed_polling_url: ''`, `embed_by_username: ''`), but every other setting in this file — including the `developer:` and `uncategorized:` sections directly above/below in the diff — declares each setting as a hash of attributes with a `default:` key (e.g. `tos_url:` -> `client: true`, `default: ...`). That nested form is what the SiteSetting YAML loader parses. The consumers added in this same PR assume these settings are properly registered: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25 reads `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:15-17 reads `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` (a boolean predicate that only exists when the setting is registered with a boolean `default:`), and lib/topic_retriever.rb:15/40/49 reads the same settings. With scalar entries the settings either fail to parse/register or get no defaults/types, so the `embeddable_host` guard can never be satisfied and the poller never fires — the whole embedding feature is broken. Fix: declare them in the nested form used by the rest of the file, e.g.

embedding:
  embeddable_host:
    default: ''
  feed_polling_enabled:
    default: false
  feed_polling_url:
    default: ''
  embed_by_username:
    default: ''

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new controller spec expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` to be called directly during the request, but the controller added in this PR enqueues the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` background job instead, so the spec's expectations are never satisfied and the test fails.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
This spec and the controller it exercises were both added by this PR and disagree about the same symbol (how `TopicRetriever` is invoked). embed_controller.rb:15 does not call `TopicRetriever` directly — it enqueues a background job, `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)`, which is handled by app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb (also in this PR) inside Sidekiq. The spec instead expects the construction to happen in-process during the request: `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. In a controller spec where `Jobs.enqueue` queues to Sidekiq rather than executing inline, `TopicRetriever.new` is never invoked, both mocha expectations are unmet, and this test fails. Fix the validator side to assert the enqueue the controller actually performs, e.g.:

it "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" do
  TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(nil)
  Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, user_id: nil, embed_url: embed_url)
  get :best, embed_url: embed_url
end

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the migration executes `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` with no check that a row was returned. WHY: site_settings only stores rows for explicitly-set values, so on any site that never set `embed_category` (the default state, including every fresh install) the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError — the migration aborts and the whole deploy fails; the `if category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 that was meant to cover this case is unreachable because a returned category id can never be 0 (serial ids start at 1) and the zero-row case crashes before reaching it. Note the same migration guards the identical pattern correctly six lines later with `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` (line 19). HOW: check the result count before indexing, e.g. `res = execute(...); category_id = res.cmd_tuples > 0 ? res[0]['id'].to_i : 0` and only then fall back to uncategorized_category_id.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting is inserted verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no normalization and unescaped SQL quoting. WHY: values in the old setting were allowed to include scheme and path — e.g. 'http://discourse.org' and 'https://example.com/1234' (exactly the forms used in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:69-70 and in the removed spec lines) — but the model strips scheme/path only on save (EmbeddableHost#before_validation), not on lookup, and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17) matches `lower(host) = uri.host`; a stored 'http://discourse.org' therefore never equals the parsed referer host 'discourse.org', so after upgrading, embedding breaks (Discourse::InvalidAccess on embed/comments and no category on TopicEmbed.import) for every host that was configured with a scheme/path until an admin re-saves each row; additionally a value containing an apostrophe breaks the interpolated INSERT. HOW: normalize each entry during the migration the same way the model does (`h.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')`) and interpolate it via `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and use the result without checking it is present. WHY: when the id does not exist (row deleted in another session, or a direct PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id), `save_host(nil)` executes `nil.host = ...` (line 23) and `destroy` executes `nil.destroy` (line 16), raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 404; `save_host` likewise reads `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without checking the `embeddable_host` param exists, so a PUT without that payload crashes the same way. HOW: look up the record with a nil guard and raise Discourse::NotFound (or render_json_error) when missing, and fall back safely when `params[:embeddable_host]` is absent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` without guarding against a nil `host`. WHY: creating or updating a host whose `host` value is omitted/null (e.g. POST /admin/embeddable_hosts with `{embeddable_host: {category_id: 4}}`) reaches `nil.sub!` and raises NoMethodError — the request returns a 500 — instead of failing the `validates_format_of :host` check with a normal validation error. HOW: return early when the host is blank (`return if self.host.blank?`) so the format validation produces a clean 422 error, or use `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...)`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Embed allowlist lookup lowercases only the stored host, never the incoming URI host (nor hosts on save), so mixed-case domains silently fail the case-insensitive host check.
suggestions.suggestionContent: record_for_host lowercases only the database side of the comparison while the incoming uri.host (case-preserving in Ruby's URI) is never downcased, and stored hosts are never normalized to lowercase on save (before_validation only strips scheme/path; the validation regex is case-insensitive). The result is an inconsistently-normalized comparison of case-insensitive domain data: any allowlisted host containing an uppercase letter — or any referer/embed URL whose hostname arrives with different casing — fails host_allowed?, so embed requests from an explicitly allowlisted host are rejected and TopicEmbed.import's category derivation (eh.try(:category_id)) silently yields nil so embedded topics go to uncategorized. Normalize both sides: downcase the input in record_for_host and downcase the host in before_validation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Migration aborts with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' setting row is absent (the default), because the result is dereferenced without an empty check and the `== 0` fallback branch is unreachable.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The category_id derivation dereferences the query result without checking that a row was returned: Discourse stores only overridden site settings, so on default installations (and fresh installs) there is no 'embed_category' row, execute(...)[0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting db:migrate for most sites. Additionally the `if category_id == 0` fallback to uncategorized_category_id is unreachable dead code — category_id is only assigned when a row WAS returned (ids start at 1) — so the intended fallback never executes, and the uncategorized query itself has the same unguarded [0]['value'] dereference.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Legacy hosts migrated verbatim (with scheme/path) bypass the model's normalization, so previously allowed hosts can never match record_for_host after upgrade.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim, but the old site setting stored full URL forms (scheme and/or path — e.g. 'http://discourse.org', 'https://example.com/1234', exactly the inputs shown in this diff's own replaced spec lines), and the model's before_validation normalization (scheme/path stripping, embeddable_host.rb:5-8) only runs on model save, never on these raw INSERTs. Post-migration, record_for_host compares lower(stored) against uri.host — which can never contain '://' or a path — so migrated entries in URL form are permanently unmatchable: previously allowed hosts silently lose embed access, and TopicEmbed.import loses their category mapping (topics land in uncategorized). Normalize each legacy value the same way the model does before inserting (strip scheme, strip path, downcase), and skip blank lines.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: topic_spec.rb keeps a test asserting expandable_first_post? is false when no embeddable host exists, but the model hunk removed that check, so the test passes only vacuously and contradicts the model's behavior under the condition its title describes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The spec hunk retains the test "is false if embeddable_host is blank", but the model hunk (app/models/topic.rb:868-870) removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard from `expandable_first_post?`, so the model no longer consults EmbeddableHost at all. As written the test passes only vacuously — it no longer fabricates a host, sets `embed_truncate`, or stubs `has_topic_embed?` (those happen only inside the nested 'with an emeddable host' describe at 1407-1412). Under the exact condition the test name describes (embed_truncate on, topic embedded, no embeddable host), the model now returns true while this test claims it should be false. Update the test to match the new contract (e.g. rename/assert the embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? conditions) or remove it, so the suite doesn't silently assert behavior deleted in this PR.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb had their contents swapped: the new file holds all the :category fabricators while the old category file now holds Fabricator(:embeddable_host).
suggestions.suggestionContent: The contents of the two files are swapped relative to their names: the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb declares the four :category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), while category_fabricator.rb was rewritten to contain Fabricator(:embeddable_host) (host "eviltrout.com", category). Fabrication loads fabricators by file content, so specs pass, but the repo now declares the wrong thing in each file: deleting or 'cleaning up' embeddable_host_fabricator.rb expecting only the embeddable host fabricator would silently wipe every category fabricator, and category_fabricator.rb misleads anyone looking for Fabricator(:category). Restore the category fabricators to category_fabricator.rb and put Fabricator(:embeddable_host) into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: PUT /admin/customize/embedding accepts and silently discards the request body, returning 200 with unchanged data; its only frontend caller is rendered by no template.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The update action declares an update endpoint but uses nothing from the request: fetch_embedding (run by before_filter before every action, including update) rebuilds @embedding fresh from the DB, so update re-serializes unchanged data and returns 200 success while discarding whatever the client sent. Its only frontend caller, saveChanges() in admin-embedding.js.es6, is not rendered by any template — embedding.hbs only renders the add-host button and the host table — so this is dead on both ends. Either apply the submitted params to real settings before rendering, or remove the PUT route (config/routes.rb:139) and the saveChanges action until there are embedding settings to persist, so clients cannot 'successfully' save nothing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Saving a newly added host overwrites the record's category with the never-initialized local categoryId (null) instead of the category the server actually assigned, leaving a blank badge on the row.
suggestions.suggestionContent: save() sets the displayed category from the local categoryId, but that property is only initialized by the edit() action — hosts added via addHost save with categoryId still null, the server fills in uncategorized_category_id (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25) and the save response updates the record's category_id, yet the component then overwrites host.category with the lookup of the stale/null local categoryId. The row ends up with a real persisted category_id but an empty {{category-badge host.category}} until the page reloads. Derive the category from the save response / record's category_id (or only perform the manual set when categoryId is present), instead of unconditionally using the possibly-never-set local value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The PR swapped the contents of the two fabricator files: category_fabricator.rb now holds only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds only the category fabricators.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The contents of the two fabricator files were swapped in this PR. spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and no category fabricator at all, while the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains exactly the four former category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) and no embeddable_host fabricator. Each file's name now contradicts its contents: someone opening category_fabricator.rb to find the :category fabricator finds the embeddable-host one instead, and vice versa. Because fabricator definitions are loaded by globbing the directory, all specs still pass, so the mistake is invisible to CI. Swap the contents back: restore the category fabricators in category_fabricator.rb and move Fabricator(:embeddable_host) into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The rewritten expandable_first_post? specs keep a test named for the embeddable-host check this PR removed from the method, and misspell 'embeddable' as 'emeddable' in the nested describe.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Topic#expandable_first_post? is now just SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed? (topic.rb:868-869 — this PR dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? clause), but the rewritten spec still names the outer test "is false if embeddable_host is blank". The method no longer consults embeddable hosts at all, so that printed test name describes behaviour that was removed: the assertion passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, and it would pass identically with an embeddable host present. Additionally, the nested describe at line 1407 misspells the domain term: 'with an emeddable host'. Rename or fold the stale outer test into the nested block, and fix 'emeddable' → 'embeddable'.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The embed_category lookup in the migration dereferences result[0] without checking for missing rows, raising NoMethodError and aborting the migration for any site whose embed_category is unset/blank.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration is the only consumer of the retired `embed_category` site setting, but it assumes a shape the old contract never guaranteed: it unconditionally dereferences `execute(...)[0]['id']` on a query that returns zero rows unless some category's `name` exactly equals the stored setting value. `TopicEmbed` fed `SiteSetting.embed_category` directly into `PostCreator`'s `category:` option (which takes an id), and sites that never configured embedding have a blank/absent row — in both cases the `INNER JOIN ... ON s.value = c.name` matches nothing, so `result[0]` is nil and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting `db:migrate` for effectively every site. Notably, the very next query in the same migration (for `embeddable_hosts`) is guarded with `cmd_tuples > 0` and `val.present?`, showing the author knew unset rows must be handled — and the intended `if category_id == 0` fallback is dead code because the nil dereference happens before it. Guard the lookup for zero rows / blank values (and consider matching on the stored id, not just `c.name`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The widened _id(s?) regex now deletes *_ids keys during hydration even when the referenced records aren't side-loaded, silently dropping attributes (e.g. subcategory_ids, muted_category_ids) that previously passed through to models intact.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Widening the hydration regex from /(.+)\_id$/ to /(.+)\_id(s?)$/ is a behaviour contract change for every payload rendered with __rest_serializer: "1": keys ending in _ids used to pass through `_hydrateEmbedded` untouched and reach the model verbatim, and they are now consumed. The new plural branch (store.js.es6:196-201) is also more aggressive than the pre-existing singular branch: when `_lookupSubType` fails to find the referenced records (no `root[pluralize(subType)]` side-load in that response), the singular branch keeps the original `X_id` key (it only deletes on success), but the plural branch always deletes `obj[k]` and writes `pluralize(subType)` — an array padded with `undefined` entries — so the caller ends up having lost both the ids and a usable object. Existing serializers already emit *_ids attributes (CategoryDetailedSerializer#subcategory_ids; UserSerializer/CurrentUserSerializer muted_category_ids/tracked_category_ids/watched_category_ids), and the PR's test changes only cover the new `color_ids` fixture, never an existing *_ids payload with no side-load. The plural branch should mirror the singular contract: only replace/delete the key when every lookup succeeded (and confirm obj[k] is an array before calling .map).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The migration indexes [0] on the query result before guarding for the empty case, so db:migrate raises NoMethodError whenever the embed_category JOIN returns zero rows (fresh installs and unconfigured sites).
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration dereferences the first row of a query result before checking that any row exists: `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` at line 9 (and the same pattern at line 15). The `if category_id == 0` fallback shows a zero-row result was anticipated, but the indexing happens first — when the JOIN returns no rows (fresh installs where site_settings/categories are empty during migrate, upgrades where embed_category was never set, or was set to a category id which can never equal c.name), `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting db:migrate for every such site. Guard the row lookup before dereferencing it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The plural hydration branch's `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code because .map always returns a truthy array, so unresolved ids become literal false entries while the original *_ids key is unconditionally deleted.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In _hydrateEmbedded's new plural branch, `hydrated || []` is dead code — `.map` always returns an array, which is truthy even when empty, so the fallback can never trigger. More importantly, unlike the singular branch's `if (hydrated)` guard, the plural branch maps `_lookupSubType` misses straight into the result as literal `false` entries, assigns that array to the pluralized attribute, and unconditionally deletes the original `*_ids` key — so a payload whose sidecar lacks the referenced records now yields `[false, ...]` records and loses the raw ids the previous behavior preserved. Additionally `obj[k].map` throws a TypeError if a `*_ids` key carries a null value, aborting hydration of the entire payload. Filter the falsy lookups and guard the value before mapping.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The migration copies old embeddable_hosts values (which legitimately contain schemes/paths like 'http://discourse.org') verbatim into the new table, so the new uri.host-based lookup can never match them and embedding breaks after upgrade.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration inserts the old embeddable_hosts setting values into the new table verbatim, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization (which strips the scheme and path) because raw SQL never runs callbacks. Old values legitimately contained schemes/paths — the pre-change spec in this very PR used 'http://discourse.org' and 'https://example.com/1234' — so after the upgrade the stored rows hold 'http://discourse.org', while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares `lower(host) = uri.host` ('discourse.org') and can never match them. Hosts that were embeddable before the upgrade get rejected with Discourse::InvalidAccess afterwards, and the migrated rows also fail the model's format validation if re-saved from the new admin UI. Apply the same normalization when migrating.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: update/destroy dereference the result of where(id:).first without a presence check, raising a 500 instead of a 404/error when the host record no longer exists.
suggestions.suggestionContent: update and destroy dereference the result of `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without a presence check; when no record matches (stale id after a concurrent delete, or a hand-crafted request), `first` returns nil and `save_host(nil)` / `host.destroy` raise NoMethodError as a 500 instead of returning a 404. `save_host` likewise assumes the `params[:embeddable_host]` key exists before reading `[:host]` and `[:category_id]`. Add explicit nil checks.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Migration inserts old embeddable_hosts values verbatim, bypassing the model's scheme/path normalizer that record_for_host's bare-hostname comparison depends on, so migrated hosts containing URLs never match and existing embeds 403 after upgrade.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration copies each old `embeddable_hosts` setting entry into the new table verbatim with a raw SQL INSERT, but every consumer added in this PR assumes a normalized bare hostname: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-18) matches `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` against a bare host like 'example.com', and the `before_validation` normalizer at embeddable_host.rb:5-8 (strip `https?://` and the path) only runs on model saves, never on raw SQL. The old setting accepted scheme+path forms (the PR's own rewritten embed_controller_spec fixtures show 'http://discourse.org' and 'https://example.com/1234' were valid entries under the old system), so migrated rows like 'http://example.com' can never match a referer host. After upgrading, previously working embeds raise Discourse::InvalidAccess (embed_controller.rb:61) and TopicEmbed imports lose their category (topic_embed.rb:36-43, `eh.try(:category_id)` → nil). Normalize each migrated value (strip `^https?://`, strip the path, downcase) before inserting — or insert through the model so the callbacks run.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Migration fallback `if category_id == 0` is unreachable: the no-match case raises NoMethodError on execute(...)[0]['id'] and aborts db:migrate before the fallback can run.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `if category_id == 0` fallback (lines 14-16) can never execute, and the scenario it was written for crashes instead. When the 'embed_category' site_settings row is absent (setting never set) or its value matches no category name, the JOIN at lines 9-11 returns zero rows, so execute(...)[0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting db:migrate before the fallback runs. When the JOIN does match, c.id is never 0 (category ids start at 1), so the branch is dead there too. Note the same file guards the identical risk correctly two queries later (line 19: `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`), showing zero-row results were expected. Guard the first query the same way — check result presence (cmd_tuples > 0 or a .try on [0]) before dereferencing, and likewise guard the uncategorized_category_id lookup at line 15.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new spec's describe block is named 'allows_embeddable_host' after the SiteSetting API this PR just deleted, while the tests inside call EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The describe string at spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb:23 reads "allows_embeddable_host" — the name of the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? helper whose final call sites this PR replaced with EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? (embed_controller.rb:61, topic_retriever.rb:16). A repo-wide grep for allows_embeddable_host now returns only this spec string, so the test name printed in output describes an API that exists nowhere in the code any more, while the assertions inside call EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?. Rename it to match the code under test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The migration retires the embeddable_hosts/embed_category site settings, but the PR leaves their site_settings.yml declarations and translated descriptions untouched, so the admin settings page still shows two controls whose text promises behaviour the code no longer implements.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This PR deletes every reader of the old settings (embed_controller.rb:61 now calls EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?, topic_retriever.rb:16 likewise, topic.rb:869 drops SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?, topic_embed.rb:43 uses the per-host category) and the migration purges their stored rows — but nothing in the PR updates config/site_settings.yml or the settings' server-locale description keys, where SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts and SiteSetting.embed_category are declared (they must be declared there, since the removed code called them). Discourse renders the admin settings page from those declarations, so admins will still be shown the 'embeddable hosts' and 'embed category' settings with descriptions saying they control embedding, while editing them now has no effect and the values they entered before are gone. Remove the two declarations and their server.en.yml description keys in this same change; otherwise the migration's DELETE only resets values and leaves the misleading settings text in place.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Removing `float: right` in favor of `margin-left: auto` breaks the header panel's right alignment in the legacy browsers the new prefixed mixins serve (IE10, 2009-spec WebKit/Moz).
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `.panel` right-alignment now depends solely on `margin-left: auto` on a flex item, but the same PR's `flexbox()` mixin (mixins.scss:100-106) serves `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` / `-ms-flexbox` to legacy browsers, and none of those implementations support auto margins for main-axis alignment (2009 spec uses `box-pack`, IE10 uses `-ms-flex-pack`). WHY: on IE10 and 2009-spec WebKit (Android stock ≤4.3, Safari ≤6, Chrome ≤20 — a large share of users when this ships) the login/user panel no longer sits at the right edge of the header; it packs to the left beside the logo, breaking the layout that the removed `float: right` handled in every browser. HOW: emit old-spec packing on `.contents` alongside the flex setup (e.g. `-webkit-box-pack: justify; -moz-box-pack: justify; -ms-flex-pack: justify;` plus `justify-content: space-between` — on legacy engines `justify` spreads the 2–3 header items so the panel lands on the right, while on modern engines the free space is absorbed by the auto margin, producing identical results), and add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` to the `align-items()` mixin so old Firefox centers instead of stretching.

suggestions.label: bug
