suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `align-items()` mixin emits the nonexistent `-ms-align-items` property (IE's prefixed property is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted on the previous line).
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the new `align-items()` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a real CSS property in any browser or IE version — the IE10/IE11 prefixed property is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted on the preceding line. WHY: it is an invalid declaration that every engine silently drops — currently harmless, but it ships dead code in a mixin whose purpose is complete prefix coverage and can mislead future maintenance into assuming IE is covered by that line. HOW: delete the `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` line (IE coverage stays correct via `-ms-flex-align`), and while here add the actually-missing legacy counterpart `-moz-box-align: $alignment` to match the `-moz-box` display value the `flexbox()` mixin serves to old Firefox.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: align-items mixin emits nonexistent `-ms-align-items`, a dead declaration no IE version consumes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, but that property does not exist in any browser or IE version — IE10's prefixed equivalent is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already declared on the line above. This is a dead declaration consumed by no engine; remove the `-ms-align-items` line.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: flexbox()/order() support 2009 -moz syntax but align-items() omits `-moz-box-align`, so old-Firefox flex containers lose their declared alignment.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The three flex mixins must cover the same vendor syntax set but disagree: `flexbox()` opts into the 2009 Mozilla syntax (`display: -moz-box`, line 102) and `order()` emits the matching 2009 property (`-moz-box-ordinal-group`, line 127), yet `align-items()` emits no `-moz-box-align` counterpart. In any engine that honors `-moz-box`, the flex container is created (e.g. `.contents`, `.small-action`) but `center`/`baseline` alignment silently never applies. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` to align-items().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: inline-flex mixin declares `-ms-inline-flexbox`, a value IE10 never supported, so it is dead in the only -ms- flexbox engine.
suggestions.suggestionContent: inline-flex() emits `display: -ms-inline-flexbox;`, but IE10 — the only engine with `-ms-` flexbox — never supported inline-flex, and `-ms-inline-flexbox` is not a recognized display value, so the declaration is dead there (the cascade falls through to the equally unsupported unprefixed `inline-flex`). It is harmless but misleading; either drop it or note that IE10 cannot be given inline flex at all.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Dropping the float layout without a block-flow fallback breaks the header in browsers without flexbox support.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The float→flexbox switch for the header removed the only positioning that works in browsers without flexbox support. `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)` are no-ops when the `flexbox()` mixin's display values are all unsupported (`.contents` stays block), so in IE9 / pre-4.4 Android stock browsers the `.panel` (hamburger, search, login buttons) stacks below the title instead of sitting at the right edge, doubling the header height — previously the floats handled those browsers. Reinstate `float: right` on `.panel` (and the `float: left` that was deleted from `.title`) as a block-flow fallback: per the flexbox spec, floats compute to `none` on flex items, so the fallback is provably inert in every browser that gets the flex layout and costs nothing there.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Duplicate downsize method definition causes ResizeEmoji job to crash with ArgumentError (5 args vs 3..4 expected).
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 duplicates and silently replaces the 4+1-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined at line 145 — Ruby has no method overloading, so the last definition wins and the first is dead code. WHY: the existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 positional arguments, which now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)` — every ResizeEmoji job (enqueued from app/models/emoji.rb:73 on emoji upload/replace) crashes and emoji are never resized. HOW: keep a single `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` definition and update resize_emoji.rb:14 to `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "100x100", opts)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Downsize loop reads tempfile.size from an fd orphaned by ImageOptim's atomic rename, so the loop never converges and the recorded upload filesize is wrong.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new downsize loop uses `tempfile.size` (line 66) as the loop condition and passes `tempfile.size` to `Upload.create_for` (line 72), but `Tempfile#size` fstats the open file descriptor's inode — which `OptimizedImage.downsize` → `convert_with` → `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` (optimized_image.rb:164) replaces by atomically renaming a temp copy over the path, orphaning the fd. WHY: after the first successful iteration the frozen stale size means the loop never observes the shrinking file (it always burns all 5 ImageMagick+ImageOptim passes on multi-MB images synchronously in the request thread even once the file is under the limit), and `Upload.create_for` records a wrong `upload.filesize` (upload.rb:124) — while sha1 and the stored bytes are computed path-based (upload.rb:106/138), so the DB can end up with a filesize (and possibly width/height from the orphaned fd via FastImage at upload.rb:71) that don't match the actually stored image. HOW: read the size from the path instead of the fd: use `File.size(tempfile.path)` both in the loop condition and as the `filesize` argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: allow_animation option is a no-op for browser uploads because the animated branch is keyed on the tempfile path extension, which Rack multipart files never have.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` argument passed to `OptimizedImage.downsize` (line 67) is a silent no-op for browser uploads, because `OptimizedImage.optimize` (optimized_image.rb:155) only selects the animated instruction set when the `from` PATH ends in `.GIF` — and Rack multipart tempfiles (the normal browser-upload path) have no extension. WHY: an animated GIF larger than max_image_size_kb is processed by the non-animated `convert #{from}[0] ... #{to}` instruction, which keeps only the first frame — the upload silently loses its animation even when the admin enabled allow_animated_thumbnails, contradicting the caller's explicit option. HOW: key the animated branch on the original filename/extension (e.g. pass the extension or an `animated:` hint in opts, or check the `filename` available in the controller) rather than on the tempfile path, since only the FileHelper.download path preserves the extension in the tempfile name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Hard-coded 10MB client cap no longer honors max_attachment_size_kb, blocking uploads sites previously allowed.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The client-side size check (and the 413 handler at line 246) now use a hard-coded `10 * 1024` KB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. WHY: for attachments there is no server-side automatic downsize (the new loop in uploads_controller.rb:64 is gated on `FileHelper.is_image?`), so a site configured with max_attachment_size_kb > 10MB silently loses the ability to receive 10–50MB attachments — users get 'file too large, max 10240 KB' even though the admin's setting allows the upload, and the displayed limit no longer matches the configured one. HOW: keep reading the per-type site setting (e.g. `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`), optionally using 10MB only as the ceiling for image types that the server will downsize.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The duplicate `downsize` definition shadows the old 4-arg form, so `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 now raises ArgumentError (given 5, expected 3..4).
suggestions.suggestionContent: Defining `downsize` twice does not create an overload — in Ruby the second definition (line 149, `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`) silently shadows the first (line 145, `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`), so the 4-positional-arg form is dead code and no longer callable. Existing consumer `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`; that call resolved to the old 4-arg form before this PR and now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)` whenever the resize-emoji job runs. Fix: keep a single `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` and update the resize_emoji.rb caller to pass the dimensions string, e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "100x100", opts)` (or delete the duplicate definition so the mismatch is caught locally).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Two definitions of self.downsize: the old 4-arg version at 145-147 is permanently shadowed by the new 3-arg version, leaving dead code and a silent signature break for any 4-arg caller.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Duplicate definition of OptimizedImage.downsize: the original 4-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (lines 145-147) was left in place when the new 3-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (lines 149-151) was added. In Ruby the later definition wins, so lines 145-147 are dead code that can never execute, and the old 4-arg interface silently no longer exists: a call like `OptimizedImage.downsize(a, b, 100, 100)` now binds `dimensions=100` and `opts=100` (an Integer), so `optimize`'s `!!opts[:allow_animation]` at line 155 raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` instead of producing the `100x100` geometry the caller asked for. The refactoring is incomplete — remove the old 4-arg `downsize` (lines 145-147) so there is exactly one definition matching the signature callers use.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Client gate and 413 message hardcode 10MB for all upload types while the server still enforces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb, so the two sides no longer agree and the error dialog names the wrong limit.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The client-side size gate now hardcodes 10MB (10 * 1024, line 182) for every upload type, but the server this same PR touches still enforces the admin-configurable limits: uploads_controller.rb:66 compares against `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, and the new downsize loop at :64 only runs for images, so oversized attachments are still rejected against `max_attachment_size_kb`. The old code read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, keeping the client gate and the server limit in agreement; now they don't — with a non-default attachment limit a file passes client validation and fails server-side, and the "file too large" dialog (also hardcoded to 10MB at line 246 in the 413 handler) tells the user a limit that is not the one actually enforced. Derive maxSizeKB from the same setting the server enforces (or special-case images, which the server now downsizes, and keep the per-type setting for attachments).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Download cap hardcoded to 10.megabytes while the method still enforces the configurable max_image_size_kb, so the two limits can disagree and API URL uploads fail silently for admins who raise the setting.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")` hardcodes the API download cap at 10MB while the rest of this method still enforces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (line 66) and `Upload.create_for` validates against that same setting. The old code passed `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, so the download cap and the enforced limit were the same value by construction; after this change they can disagree — with `max_image_size_kb` raised above 10MB, URL-based API uploads of images between 10MB and the setting fail silently inside the `rescue nil` and fall through to `Upload.create_for` with a nil tempfile. Keep the cap tied to the setting it is meant to mirror.

suggestions.label: CRITICAL: duplicate `downsize` definition breaks existing caller with ArgumentError and malformed ImageMagick dimensions
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Duplicate method definition at optimized_image.rb:149-151 overrides the new 5-arg signature, causing ArgumentError in resize_emoji job and potentially malformed dimensions string.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The PR adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at lines 149-151 directly after the rewritten 5-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at lines 145-147. In Ruby the later definition silently replaces the earlier one, so the effective signature accepts at most 4 positional args. An existing caller at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 positional args, which now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)` as soon as the emoji resize job runs. Even if it survived, `dimensions` would bind to the Integer 100 and be interpolated into the ImageMagick instructions as "100" instead of "100x100".

suggestions.label: Downsize loop may silently fail to reduce images larger than ~3x the size limit
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The 5-pass 80% resize loop cannot reliably bring oversized images under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, violating the stated auto-reduction invariant.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new downsize loop (lines 40-95) only exits with tempfile.size <= max when 5 successive `-resize 80%` passes suffice (0.8^5 ≈ 32.8% of the original). Pixel-dimension shrinking does not guarantee proportional file-size shrinking (e.g. PNG), so for images > ~3x SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb the loop silently gives up and Upload.create_for receives an over-limit file. The declared invariant that uploads are "automatically reduced to allowed size" is therefore not guaranteed, though the failure path is subsequently handled by validation errors.

suggestions.label: FileHelper.download cap hardcoded at 10.megabytes, inconsistent with configurable size limit
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The 10MB FileHelper.download cap at uploads_controller.rb:55 is hardcoded instead of derived from SiteSetting, mismatching admin-configurable limits.
suggestions.suggestionContent: FileHelper.download in the new downsize path is capped at 10.megabytes (line 55), matching the client-side 10MB hardcode in utilities.js:182/246. This pins the server-side download cap to a constant rather than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so raising the admin-configured limit above 10MB still downloads at most 10MB, inconsistent with the configurable limit the downsize loop targets.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: downsize is defined twice; the edited definition's max_width/max_height parameter names describe a method that is dead, silently shadowed by the new dimensions-based definition.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This PR modifies the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) to build "#{max_width}x#{max_height}", but also adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (lines 149-151). Ruby has no method overloading: the second definition silently replaces the first, so the `max_width, max_height` parameter names on the definition this PR edited describe a contract that no longer exists at runtime — any caller invoking `downsize(from, to, w, h)` has its 4th argument silently bound to `opts` (a TypeError at optimized_image.rb:155 when `opts[:allow_animation]` is evaluated on an Integer). Remove the shadowed width/height definition (or keep only one signature), so the surviving method's parameter names state what it actually receives — compare `resize` (lines 141-143), which correctly keeps the width/height signature and converts to the dimensions string internally.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new comment promises images "will be automatically reduced to allowed size", but the 5-attempt 80% loop can exit with the file still over the limit.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment added at line 63 — "allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced to allowed size" — states a guarantee the loop below does not deliver. The loop performs at most 5 downsizes of 80% each and then exits regardless of the result: with a site limit of e.g. max_image_size_kb=512, a ~10MB PNG is only reduced to ~10MB × 0.64⁵ ≈ 1.07MB, still over the limit, and is then rejected by Upload.create_for. It is also not guaranteed when `convert` fails (OptimizedImage.convert_with returns false without raising, so the file never shrinks). Reword the comment to describe what the code does ("attempt to reduce large images by repeatedly downsizing") or change the loop so the comment's claim actually holds (e.g. iterate until the size is within the limit, bounded by a minimum geometry).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The file-too-large alert now hard-codes a 10240 KB limit into the user-facing message while the server still enforces the configurable SiteSetting limit from this same PR.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The user-facing alert for a rejected upload now always claims "maximum size is 10240 KB" (the hard-coded `10 * 1024` at lines 246 and 182), but this same PR's server side still enforces the configurable limit — uploads_controller.rb:66 checks SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, and attachments are validated against their own site setting. On any site whose max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb differs from 10MB, the message shown to the user is simply false: the server rejected the file at a lower limit while the alert quotes 10240 KB. Previously the message interpolated Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb / ['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], matching what the app actually enforced. Restore the site-setting lookup (at minimum for the 413 case at line 246, which fires precisely when the server has rejected the file) so the message tells the user the real limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Two conflicting `downsize` definitions were left in optimized_image.rb; Ruby's last-definition-wins makes the width/height version dead and silently breaks the old positional calling contract.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The PR modified the original 5-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at lines 145-147 and then added a second, incompatible-signature `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at lines 149-151. Ruby keeps the last definition, so the width/height version is dead code, and any existing caller using the old positional contract is broken: a 4-arg call `downsize(from, to, w, h)` binds the height Integer into `opts`, making `opts[:allow_animation]`/`opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` raise TypeError and degrading the geometry to a width-only string ("196" instead of "196x196"), while a 5-arg call raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments 5 for 3..4). Keep exactly one definition (the string-dimensions one used by UploadsController#create_upload) and port any old-signature callers to pass a geometry string.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The 5×80% compress loop in create_upload cannot guarantee the file reaches max_image_size_kb and ignores downsize failures, so oversized files still reach Upload.create_for and the promised auto-reduction silently fails.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The resize loop assumes five 80% linear downsizes always bring an image under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, and it ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s false return value (which `convert_with` yields when `convert` fails). Boundary arithmetic: each pass reduces file size to roughly 64% (0.8² area), so after the 5 allowed attempts the floor is ~0.64^5 ≈ 10.7% of the original — a ~10MB upload (permitted by the new hardcoded 10MB client cap) against a 512KB limit ends the loop at ~1.07MB, still oversized, and is then handed to Upload.create_for, which rejects it; if `convert` fails, the loop burns 5 attempts and submits the untouched original. Bound the loop by re-checking the actual resulting size and abort early when downsize returns false, or compute the target percentage from the actual size ratio instead of a fixed "80%".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: optimized_image.rb declares two conflicting downsize contracts while uploads_controller.rb's new call matches only one of them — the two changed files agree solely via Ruby's silent last-definition-wins.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This PR leaves TWO conflicting declarations of the same method: line 145 `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (whose body builds "#{max_width}x#{max_height}") and line 149 `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. The new call added in uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` — matches only the second. The two changed files currently agree only by accident of Ruby's silent last-definition-wins: the 4-arg version is dead code, and if the duplicate is ever cleaned up by keeping the 4-arg form (the natural reading, since the 3-arg one duplicates it), the controller's "80%" binds to max_width and the opts hash to max_height, yielding invalid ImageMagick geometry like `-resize 80%x{:allow_animation=>true}>` so the auto-shrink loop silently fails on every large-image upload. Conversely, any pre-existing caller of the old 4-arg form now resolves against the 3-arg definition and crashes inside downsize_instructions (`opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` on an Integer → TypeError). Keep exactly one definition — the dimensions-string form the controller uses — and delete the stale 4-arg one.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The controller passes the percentage "80%" to OptimizedImage.downsize, but the animated-GIF path it enables via allow_animation forwards it to gifsicle's --resize-fit, which requires explicit WxH dimensions.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The auto-shrink loop passes the percentage "80%" to OptimizedImage.downsize together with `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. For ordinary images the value reaches ImageMagick's `-resize 80%\>` (downsize_instructions), which accepts percentages. But when allow_animated_thumbnails is on and the source path ends in .GIF, the model's optimize routing (optimized_image.rb:155) sends it to downsize_instructions_animated → resize_instructions_animated, which interpolates the value into gifsicle's `--resize-fit #{dimensions}` (line 120) — gifsicle requires explicit WxH geometry and does not understand percentages, so the command exits non-zero, convert_with returns false, the loop burns all 5 attempts without shrinking the file, and the oversized upload is then rejected by the model instead of being reduced. This is unreachable for normal multipart uploads (Rack tempfiles carry no file extension), but plausibly reachable through the API URL branch in this same hunk (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`), where the downloaded tempfile can retain the URL's .gif suffix. Either pass dimensions acceptable to both consumers (e.g. derive explicit WxH, or branch the animated path) or skip the animated route in this loop.

suggestions.label: Client-side 10MB hardcode decoupled from server SiteSetting size limits
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Hardcoded 10MB checks in utilities.js (lines 182, 246) and uploads_controller.rb:55 will reject valid uploads if admin raises limits above 10MB.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The client now hardcodes 10MB at line 182 and in the 413 handler at line 246, decoupling the client-side check from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb. An admin who raises the image limit above 10MB gets client-side rejections of uploads the server (and the new downsize loop) would accept. The corresponding server-side cap in FileHelper.download at uploads_controller.rb:55 is likewise pinned at 10.megabytes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Off-by-one in totalPages shows an extra blank page for groups whose member count is a multiple of the page size
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`, which overstates the page count by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. WHY: with 50 members and limit 50, totalPages is 2, so `showingLast` is false on page 1; the `next` action (line 33) then sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count) = 50`, the server returns an empty members page, and the admin sees a blank "2/2" page — the same happens for 100/150/… member groups. HOW: use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and clamp `next`'s offset to `(totalPages - 1) * limit` instead of `user_count`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: add_members lost the old `expected - current` dedupe, so re-adding an existing member hits the unique index and produces an unhandled 500 with a silent UI
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for every typed username without diffing against current membership, where `Group#add` is `self.users.push(user)` (group.rb:272-274) into a `has_many :users, through: :group_users` whose join table has a UNIQUE index on (group_id, user_id) (group_user.rb:18) and no uniqueness validation. WHY: the removed code this PR replaced (`usernames=` setter, group.rb:244-264) computed `additions = expected - current` so re-adding an existing member was impossible; now an admin who re-types a username that is already a member (easy to do since the member list is paginated to 50 rows and the selector is never cleared, admin-group.js:62) triggers a duplicate GroupUser INSERT that raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique — an unhandled 500 (the `if group.save / render_json_error` fallback never runs), and the client-side `addMembers` has no error handler so the failure is silent. HOW: skip users already in the group before adding, e.g. `group.user_ids.include?(user.id)` check, or reuse the diff logic from the old `usernames=` setter (pass the full expected list and let it diff).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: remove_member bypasses the GroupUser destroy path, losing primary_group_id cleanup and risking a stale user_count counter cache
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` which removes the join record directly, bypassing the removal bookkeeping that the deleted `usernames=` + `after_save :destroy_deletions` flow performed (group.rb:257-260 and 287-295): GroupUser `gu.destroy` (which keeps the `counter_cache: "user_count"` column accurate — group_user.rb:2) and the explicit `primary_group_id = NULL` cleanup (`User.where('id = ? AND primary_group_id = ?', gu.user_id, gu.group_id).update_all 'primary_group_id = NULL'`). WHY: nothing in the new action or the GroupUser model (read — bare `belongs_to`, no callbacks) nulls `primary_group_id`, so removing a user whose primary group is this group (settable via the admin user page, admin/users_controller.rb:135) leaves the user with a dangling `primary_group_id` pointing at a group they no longer belong to; additionally, if Rails removes the join via delete_all-style SQL (plain :through `delete` without a `dependent` on the join), `group.user_count` never decrements and stays stale in the admin groups index (BasicGroupSerializer) until counters are reset. The spec only asserts `group.users.count == 0` (a live COUNT query), so both regressions pass the test. HOW: remove membership by destroying the join record, e.g. `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).each(&:destroy)` plus the primary_group_id nulling from `destroy_deletions`, or set `group.usernames = group.usernames.split(",") - [user.username]`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new controller specs pass group_id directly, bypassing routing, so they mask the :id vs :group_id parameter mismatch and keep the suite green while the endpoints 400 in production
suggestions.suggestionContent: The rewritten `.add_members` and `.remove_member` specs pass `group_id:` directly to the controller (`xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id`), which bypasses routing entirely and encodes the wrong parameter name — the member routes actually deliver the group id as `id`, so these specs stay green while every real request to the endpoints fails with 400. Once the controller is corrected to `params[:id]`, update these specs to pass `id: group.id` (or convert them to request specs that go through the route) so the routing/controller parameter contract is actually exercised.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, so the admin-visible 'page x/y' text and the showingLast guard overshoot by one page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, letting "next" navigate onto an empty member list.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The totalPages computed property returns Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one page too many whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50 → "3" total pages when there are 2). This value is shown to the admin as the "{{currentPage}}/{{totalPages}}" text in group.hbs and feeds showingLast, which is therefore false on the actual last page — the "next" link stays enabled and the next action clamps the offset to user_count, landing the admin on an empty members page captioned "3/3". Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead (and cap the next offset so it can never equal user_count), so the displayed pagination text and the showingLast name agree with reality.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: totalPages uses floor+1 instead of ceil, creating a phantom empty last page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50 → totalPages 3 when only 2 pages exist). Since `showingLast` compares currentPage to totalPages, the `next` action stays enabled on the real last page, and its clamp `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` (line 33) plus the offset clamp in Group#findMembers (group.js line 23) let the offset reach exactly user_count — so the admin navigates to a blank members list displayed as "3/3" and is stranded there (next is finally disabled). Use Math.ceil so the page count matches the actual pages.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The remove_member spec issues PUT while the route added in this PR maps remove_member to DELETE (and the sibling test at line 125 uses DELETE).
suggestions.suggestionContent: This PR adds the route `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (routes.rb), and the sibling test at line 125 correctly uses `xhr :delete, :remove_member`. The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" test at line 115 instead issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`. The two sites that must agree (route verb vs test verb) disagree. It only passes because Rails controller specs dispatch to the action without exercising routing; converted to a request spec (or if the verb is ever enforced) this test would fail with a routing error. Align the verb with the DELETE route.

suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym raises on nil, making the .compact nil-guard dead code that crashes every translation instead of skipping the site locale.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises NoMethodError when default_locale is nil, so the trailing `.compact` is dead code — it can never filter a nil, and the nil-tolerance it clearly intends (skip the site locale, keep English) is impossible. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Fallback locales are only ensured-loaded in the web controller, so background jobs iterate an unloaded fallback chain and emit 'translation missing' instead of English fallbacks.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` is only ever invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale (application_controller.rb:159), so background job processes — which set `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` at app/jobs/base.rb:151 and switch locales via `I18n.with_locale` (lib/post_destroyer.rb:102) — never load the fallback locales. HOW: also invoke `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` after setting/switching the locale in app/jobs/base.rb (around line 151), e.g. right after `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`, or preload the fallback chain when the job process boots.

suggestions.suggestionContent: FallbackLocaleList#[] makes every backend translation result depend on the mutable SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache (translate_accelerator.rb:72) keys entries only on "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}" — the fallback chain is not part of the key. (which resets @loaded_locales and @cache in translate_accelerator.rb:39-43).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new fallback chain makes translate results depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's LRU cache key omits it, so stale fallback translations are served after a default_locale change.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Adding the fallback chain changes the behaviour contract of I18n.translate: a translation's result is no longer a function of (key, locale, backend) only, but also of SiteSetting.default_locale, since the Fallbacks backend resolves missing keys from [locale, default_locale, :en] (i18n.rb:17). suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The initializer feeds Symbol locales (:en, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym) into I18n.ensure_loaded!, whose load_locale regex requires a String name, so fallback locale files are never actually loaded.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new `ensure_loaded!(locale)` does not hold up the premise of its cross-file caller. config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 (`FallbackLocaleList#[]`) produces the fallback locales as Symbols — `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` and the hardcoded `:en` — and i18n.rb:21 feeds them to `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Device-limit rejection poisons the localCache, denying the first request then admitting all retries for 29 minutes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new error propagation makes the device limit deny a new device's first request, but tagDeviceUI caches the device key (impl.go:87, set BEFORE the store call) even when the store rejects it, so the next request hits the cache (impl.go:83) and is silently granted anonymous access. WHY: A device beyond the limit is denied exactly once and then admitted for the next 29 minutes without ever being recorded — the limit enforcement is both flaky (first request fails) and trivially bypassable with a single retry, defeating the feature's purpose. HOW: Only set the localCache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (or remove the cache entry / return the limit error before caching), so rejected devices are re-evaluated against the store on every request.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Count-then-upsert without a transaction or lock lets concurrent new devices overshoot the configured limit.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The device-limit check in CreateOrUpdateDevice is a check-then-act with no transaction or locking — CountDevices runs in a separate DB session from the subsequent upsert. WHY: Concurrent requests from new anonymous devices (the exact burst scenario the limit targets) all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, so the configured limit is silently exceeded; the limit is a soft advisory, not an enforcement. HOW: Wrap the count and the upsert in a single transaction with a locking read (e.g. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / advisory lock) or enforce the cap atomically in the INSERT statement so overshoot is impossible.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The device limit only gates requests carrying the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header, so omitting the header bypasses it entirely.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new device limit is enforced only for requests that carry the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header; TagDevice returns nil when the header is absent (impl.go:119-122) and client.go:52-58 still returns a full anonymous identity. WHY: Any client (scraper, load generator, scripted abuse) that simply omits the header is granted unlimited anonymous access while being neither counted against the limit nor recorded — the limit provides no protection against the abuse it is meant to cap. HOW: Derive the device identifier server-side (e.g. issue an anonymous device cookie on first visit) instead of relying solely on an optional client-supplied header, so the limit applies to all anonymous requests.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Anonymous auth now blocks on a DB COUNT plus write per cache miss, with the previous 2-minute timeout removed.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: TagDevice was moved from an asynchronous fire-and-forget goroutine (2-minute timeout on a Background context) into the synchronous authn hot path at client.go:44. WHY: Every anonymous request on a localCache miss (every new device, every ~29 minutes per existing device, and per instance in HA since the cache is per-process) now performs a COUNT(*) plus a write before the request is authorized, and the removed 2-minute timeout means a slow or unresponsive database now directly stalls all anonymous traffic — the highest-volume unauthenticated path (public/embedded dashboards). HOW: Keep the write off the request path (e.g. re-introduce the bounded-timeout background tagging) and enforce the limit with an explicit, time-boxed check, so anonymous availability no longer depends on anon_device write latency.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before the DB write and never evicts it on failure, so on this PR's new ErrDeviceLimitReached path the first request from a beyond-limit device fails while every retry within 29 minutes succeeds without the device ever being recorded.
suggestions.suggestionContent: tagDeviceUI writes the local-cache entry (impl.go:87) before the DB write and never evicts it on failure. With this PR's new failure path (CreateOrUpdateDevice → ErrDeviceLimitReached, database.go:96; propagated by the new `return err` at impl.go:147 and client.go:46-47 `return nil, err`), the cache is poisoned for 29 minutes: the FIRST request from a new beyond-limit device fails authentication, then every subsequent request within the 29-minute TTL hits the cache at impl.go:83-85 and returns nil — the device is granted anonymous access without ever being persisted or counted. The limit is deterministically bypassed by retrying, and legitimate users get one intermittent failed request per window per instance. Evict the cache key (a.localCache.Delete(key)) when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns an error, or only cache after a successful write.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert across two separate DB sessions, so concurrent requests from new devices can both pass the count and both insert, permanently exceeding the configured limit.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new limit check in CreateOrUpdateDevice is a check-then-act race: CountDevices (database.go:110) runs in its own DB session and the INSERT/UPSERT at database.go:149-153 runs in a different session — there is no transaction, lock, or constraint tying them together. Two concurrent requests from two new devices can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit; since existing devices are always allowed to update (database.go:115-116), the overshoot persists as long as those devices stay active in the 30-day window. Make the guard atomic, e.g. a single conditional INSERT ... SELECT with a COUNT subquery per dialect, or a transaction that takes an exclusive lock (advisory lock / serializable isolation) around count+insert.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateDevice treats rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached, but a matched existing device can yield 0 rows via clock skew beyond the 1-minute window or MySQL's changed-rows semantics, falsely rejecting legitimate anonymous users.
suggestions.suggestionContent: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever rowsAffected == 0, but 0 rows does not only mean "new device, limit reached": (a) a legitimate existing device whose stored updated_at sits outside [UpdatedAt-30d, UpdatedAt+1min] (database.go:78-81) — e.g. clock skew >1 min between HA instances, since updated_at is stamped from each instance's own clock — is falsely rejected with the limit error, surfacing as intermittent auth failures via client.go:46-47; (b) on MySQL, RowsAffected reports *changed* rows by default, so a matched-but-identical UPDATE (same second, same client_ip/user_agent from another pod, each with its own local cache) also yields 0 → false ErrDeviceLimitReached for an already-counted device. Separate "row not found" from the limit-enforcement decision (e.g. explicit existence check, wider/monotonic window keyed on the stored value, or dialect-aware affected-rows handling).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The TS contract declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined`, implying the key can be absent/undefined when no limit is configured, but the producing Go DTO (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195, `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` with json tag "anonymousDeviceLimit" and no omitempty) always serializes the field — emitting 0 when unset (default 0 from setting.go:1654). The `undefined` case can therefore never occur at runtime, and "no limit" is represented as 0 on the wire while the type suggests undefined, so a frontend check like `config.anonymousDeviceLimit === undefined` can never detect the unconfigured case. Align the two sides: either make the Go field `*int64` with `json:"anonymousDeviceLimit,omitempty"` so it is genuinely omitted when unset, or narrow the TS type to `number` and document 0 as "no limit".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateDevice treats MySQL's rows-changed count of 0 as "device not found", wrongly returning ErrDeviceLimitReached for an existing device whose stored values are unchanged.
suggestions.suggestionContent: updateDevice infers "device does not exist / limit reached" from result.RowsAffected() == 0 (database.go:95-97). On MySQL, RowsAffected() reports rows *changed*, not rows *matched* (Grafana's default DSN does not enable CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS). A row that matches the WHERE clause but whose client_ip, user_agent and updated_at are already identical to the values being written reports 0 affected rows. Since updated_at is truncated to seconds in MySQL (see the comment at impl.go:69) and the localCache guard in tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-87) is not atomic across concurrent goroutines, two simultaneous requests from the same device (anonymous dashboards fire several concurrent API calls) can both reach updateDevice with the same second-precision timestamp and identical IP/UA; the second returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that exists and is well within the limit, and client.go then rejects the anonymous request. Check existence explicitly (e.g., a SELECT/EXISTS for device_id within the window, or reuse the upsert path used when under the limit) rather than inferring absence from a zero changed-row count.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The behavior added in this PR makes the AnonStore interface doc comment stale: "// CreateOrUpdateDevice creates or updates a device." (database.go:42-43). When a device limit is configured and the active-device count has reached it, the function no longer creates anything — for a device_id not already present it returns the sentinel ErrDeviceLimitReached (via updateDevice's zero-rowsAffected path at lines 95-97), which client.go's Authenticate relies on via errors.Is to reject the anonymous request. A caller reading the interface contract has no way to know the limit behavior or that this error exists. Update the comment to document that, when a device limit is set and reached, only existing recently-updated devices are refreshed and a new device yields ErrDeviceLimitReached.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new doc comment on updateDevice misdescribes the function it was added for: "updates a device if it exists and has been updated between the given times." No times are "given" — the signature takes only ctx and device, and the 30-day-lower/1-minute-upper window is computed internally (lines 80-82) from device.UpdatedAt, so a reader of the signature cannot reconcile the comment. Worse, the comment omits the primary failure contract: when the WHERE clause matches zero rows the function returns the sentinel ErrDeviceLimitReached (lines 95-97) rather than silently doing nothing, and that sentinel is exactly what the anonymous auth client branches on (client.go errors.Is). Rewrite the comment to state the real condition (device exists and its updated_at falls within [UpdatedAt−30d, UpdatedAt+1m]) and document that zero matched rows yields ErrDeviceLimitReached.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Write lock acquired without re-checking the cache serializes redundant manifest reads on cold start and serializes every Dev-mode call across disk I/O.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The write lock is acquired without re-checking the cache, so the double-checked-locking pattern is missing its second check. WHAT: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` (webassets.go:48), the code never re-reads `entryPointAssetsCache` before doing the expensive work. WHY: on a non-Dev cold start, every request that observed a nil cache queues on the exclusive lock and each one serially performs the full `os.Open` + JSON decode of assets-manifest.json and `SetContentDeliveryURL` (lines 60-69) — N redundant serialized reads instead of 1 read + N-1 cache returns; worse, in Dev mode (`cfg.Env == setting.Dev`) the fast path never short-circuits, so EVERY call — each index page render (pkg/api/index.go:82), frontend settings call (pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62), and panic recovery (pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141) — takes the exclusive write lock and holds it across disk I/O, fully serializing all concurrent consumers where they previously ran in parallel. HOW: re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock: `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, which collapses the cold-start stampede to a single read and lets Dev-mode cache hits skip the exclusive lock entirely.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The double-checked locking is missing its second check: concurrent cold-start requests in non-Dev each serialize on the write lock and rebuild the asset manifest, redundantly overwriting the cache.
suggestions.suggestionContent: After acquiring the write lock at line 48, the cache is never re-checked, so every request that missed the RLock fast path performs the full assets-manifest.json read and JSON parse, even when another goroutine has already populated the cache. Complete the double-checked locking pattern by re-reading the cache under the write lock and returning early when it is populated (non-Dev). This avoids N serial rebuilds during cold start while preserving correctness (each build is equivalent, so this is redundant work, not corruption).

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Missing re-check of the cache after acquiring the write lock makes every concurrent cold-start caller re-read and re-parse the manifest while serialized on the mutex, and holds the exclusive lock across file I/O for every Dev-mode request.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The write-lock acquisition has no second cache check, so the double-checked locking is incomplete. In non-Dev mode, every concurrent cold-start caller that queued on the write lock (webassets.go:48) redoes the full assets-manifest read and JSON parse (lines 60-66) even though the first one already populated entryPointAssetsCache — with N concurrent first requests, the work is done N times while they serialize on the mutex. In Dev mode it is worse: the fast path is skipped by design, so every request takes the process-wide exclusive lock and holds it across the os.Open/JSON-decode disk I/O (readWebAssetsFromFile, lines 73-83), serializing all concurrent requests to the index/frontendsettings endpoints. Re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, and ideally compute `result` into a local outside the lock so the lock is only held for the cache store.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: TestLogger.FromContext returns a detached new logger, so logs emitted through the new FromContext-based path are invisible to tests holding the original TestLogger.
suggestions.suggestionContent: TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() — a brand-new detached instance — instead of the receiver, so log calls made through the FromContext-based path are recorded on an instance the test never holds. LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) (logger_middleware.go:58), so any test injecting a TestLogger to assert on "Plugin Request Completed" (call count, message, ctx attrs) will observe zero recorded calls and silently pass/fail against an empty recorder. suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The request-size assertions observe an always-zero payload, so a broken size computation in instrumentPluginRequestSize would keep the test green.
